translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 234
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 234

sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十】起玄黓涒灘，盡閼逢閹茂五月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 50] Beginning in the year xuantuan, ending in the fifth month of the year yanmao; in all, a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 50] From the xuantuan year through the fifth month of the yanmao year—a span of somewhat more than two years.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝九貞元八年（

translations.literal: The Divine Martial and Sagely Literary Emperor Dezong, eighth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of the Tang, eighth year of the Zhenyuan era (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元七九二年）

translations.literal: ren-shen, CE 792)
translations.idiomatic: ren-shen, 792 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，壬寅，執夢沖，數其罪而斬之。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, day ren-yin; Meng Chong was seized, his crimes were enumerated, and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the ren-yin day of the second month, Meng Chong was arrested; his offenses were read out, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 雲南之路始通。

translations.literal: The road to Yunnan was opened for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Communications with Yunnan were established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，山南東道節度使曹成王皋薨。

translations.literal: Third month, day ding-chou; Cao, Prince of Cao, Wang Gao, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the ding-chou day, Wang Gao, Prince of Cao and governor of Shannan East Circuit, passed away.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使劉玄佐有威略，每李納使至，玄佐厚結之，故常得其陰事，先為之備。

translations.literal: The Xuanwu military governor Liu Xuanzuo had prestige and stratagem; whenever Li Na's envoys arrived, Xuanzuo treated them generously, and therefore often learned their secret affairs and prepared against them in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo of Xuanwu was formidable and resourceful; he lavishly cultivated Li Na's messengers and thus routinely learned their master's confidential plans before they could act.

sentences.zh: 納憚之。

translations.literal: Na feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na was wary of him.

sentences.zh: 其母雖貴，日織絹一匹，謂玄佐曰：「汝本寒微，天子富貴汝至此，必以死報之！」

translations.literal: Though his mother was honored, every day she wove a bolt of silk, and said to Xuanzuo: "You were originally of humble station; the Son of Heaven enriched and ennobled you to this point—you must repay it with your life!"
translations.idiomatic: Though exalted as his mother, she still wove a bolt of silk each day and told Xuanzuo: "You rose from poverty; the emperor raised you to wealth and rank—you owe him your life in service!"

sentences.zh: 故玄佐始終不失臣節。

translations.literal: Therefore Xuanzuo from beginning to end never lost the deportment of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: It was for this reason that Liu Xuanzuo never once failed in loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 庚午，玄佐薨。

translations.literal: Day geng-wu; Xuanzuo died.
translations.idiomatic: On the geng-wu day, Liu Xuanzuo died.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度判官李實知留後事，性刻薄，裁損軍士衣食。

translations.literal: The Shannan East Circuit regent Li Shi knew remaining-affairs affairs; his nature was harsh and mean, and he curtailed the soldiers' food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, who as regent of Shannan East Circuit handled routine administration, was harsh by nature and cut the troops' food and clothing allowances.

sentences.zh: 鼓角將楊清潭帥眾作亂。

translations.literal: The drum-and-horn commandant Yang Qingtan led the masses in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The drum-and-horn officer Yang Qingtan led his men in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 夜焚掠城中，獨不犯曹王皋家。

translations.literal: By night they set fire and plundered within the city, but did not violate the household of Prince of Cao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: That night they burned and looted the city, yet spared the residence of Prince of Cao Gao.

sentences.zh: 實逾城走免。

translations.literal: Shi fled over the wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi escaped over the city wall.

sentences.zh: 明旦，都將徐誠縋城而入，號令禁遏，然後止。

translations.literal: At dawn, the chief commander Xu Cheng was lowered by rope into the city; he issued orders forbidding and restraining, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Chief Commander Xu Cheng was lowered into the city by rope; once he proclaimed orders forbidding further violence, the rioting ceased.

sentences.zh: 收清潭等六人斬之。

translations.literal: They seized Qingtan and six others and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtan and six accomplices were arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 實歸京師，以為司農少卿。

translations.literal: Shi returned to the capital and was made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi returned to the capital and was appointed vice minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 實，元慶之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Shi was the great-grandson of Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was a great-grandson of Li Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以荊南節度使樊澤為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Day bing-zi; Fan Ze, military governor of Jingnan, was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the bing-zi day, Fan Ze, governor of Jingnan, was transferred to govern Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，竇參為度支轉運使，班宏副之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dou Can was commissioner of the revenue and transport circuit, with Ban Hong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dou Can had served as commissioner of revenue and transport, with Ban Hong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 參許宏，俟一歲以使職歸之。

translations.literal: Can promised Hong that after one year he would return the commissionership to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can had promised Hong that after a year he would hand the commission back to him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，參無歸意，宏怒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Can showed no intention of returning; Hong was angry.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a year passed with no sign that Can would step aside, Hong grew furious.

sentences.zh: 司農少卿張滂，宏所薦也，參欲使滂分主江、淮鹽鐵，宏不可。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries Zhang Pang was one whom Hong had recommended; Can wished to have Pang take charge separately of the Jiang-Huai salt and iron, but Hong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang, vice minister of the Imperial Granaries, had been Hong's own nominee, yet Dou Can wanted Pang to take over the Jiang-Huai salt and iron monopoly separately—an arrangement Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 滂知之，亦怨宏。

translations.literal: Pang learned of this and also resented Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang learned of this, he too came to resent Hong.

sentences.zh: 及參為上所疏，乃讓度支使於宏，又不欲利權專歸於宏，乃薦滂於上。

translations.literal: When Can was impeached by the emperor, he then yielded the revenue commissionership to Hong; yet not wishing all profit-making authority to fall solely to Hong, he recommended Pang to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Can fell out of favor with the emperor, he yielded the revenue commission to Hong; but unwilling to let Hong monopolize all lucrative authority, he recommended Zhang Pang to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以宏判度支，以滂為戶部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使，仍隸於宏以悅之。

translations.literal: Hong was made acting commissioner of revenue; Pang was made Vice Minister of Revenue and salt-and-iron transport commissioner, yet still subordinate to Hong to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong was appointed acting revenue commissioner; Zhang Pang became vice minister of revenue and salt-and-iron transport commissioner, but was left nominally under Hong's authority as a conciliatory gesture.

sentences.zh: 竇參陰狡而愎，恃權而貪，每遷除，多與族子給事中申議之。

translations.literal: Dou Can was secretive, crafty, and obstinate; relying on power he was greedy; for every appointment or removal he often deliberated with his clansman, Supervising Secretary Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can was secretive, obstinate, and greedy with power; on nearly every appointment or dismissal he consulted his kinsman Dou Shen, a supervising secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 申招權受賂，時人謂之「喜鵲」。

translations.literal: Shen grasped power and accepted bribes; people of the time called him the "Magpie."
translations.idiomatic: Shen traded on his influence for bribes, and contemporaries nicknamed him "Magpie."

sentences.zh: 上頗聞之，謂參曰：「申必為卿累，宜出之以息物議。」

translations.literal: The emperor had heard much of this and said to Can: "Shen will surely be a burden to you; you ought to send him out to quiet public criticism."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had heard of this and told Can: "Shen is bound to become your liability; you should post him elsewhere to quiet public criticism."

sentences.zh: 參再三保其無他，申亦不悛。

translations.literal: Can repeatedly vouched that Shen had no other designs, but Shen also did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can repeatedly assured him that Shen meant no harm, yet Shen showed no sign of reform.

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍虢王則之，巨之子也，與申善，左諫議大夫、知制誥吳通玄與陸贄不葉，竇申恐贄進用，陰與通玄、則之作謗書以傾贄。

translations.literal: Left Golden Crow Guards Grand General Prince of Guo Zezhi, son of Ju, was on good terms with Shen; Left Remonstrance Grandee and drafter of edicts Wu Tongxuan was at odds with Lu Zhi; Dou Shen feared Zhi's advancement and secretly joined with Tongxuan and Zezhi to compose slanderous writings to overthrow Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guo Zezhi, son of Li Ju and grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guards, was close to Shen; Wu Tongxuan, left remonstrance grandee and drafter of edicts, was hostile to Lu Zhi. Fearing Lu Zhi's rise, Dou Shen secretly conspired with Wu and Zezhi to circulate libels aimed at bringing Zhi down.

sentences.zh: 上皆察知其狀。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived the full situation in each case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁亥，貶則之昭州司馬，通玄泉州司馬，申道州司馬。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day ding-hai; Zezhi was demoted to military adjutant of Zhaozhou, Tongxuan to military adjutant of Quanzhou, Shen to military adjutant of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the ding-hai day of the fourth month, Zezhi was demoted to adjutant of Zhaozhou, Tongxuan to adjutant of Quanzhou, and Shen to adjutant of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋賜通玄死。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Tongxuan was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor ordered Wu Tongxuan to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐之喪，將佐匿之，稱疾請代，上亦為之隱，遣使即軍中問：「以陝虢觀察使吳湊為代可乎？」

translations.literal: At Liu Xuanzuo's death, his officers concealed it, claiming illness and requesting a replacement; the emperor also concealed it for them and sent an envoy to the army to ask: "Would it be acceptable to replace him with Wu Cou, commissioner of Shaan-Guo?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuanzuo died, his officers hid the fact, reported him ill, and asked the court for a successor; the emperor went along with the deception and sent an envoy to the camp to ask: "Would Wu Cou, commissioner of Shaan-Guo, be acceptable as his replacement?"

sentences.zh: 監軍孟介、行軍司馬盧瑗皆以為便，然後除之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Meng Jie and the chief of staff Lu Yuan all said it would be convenient, and only then was the appointment made.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Meng Jie and chief of staff Lu Yuan both approved, and only then was the appointment issued.

sentences.zh: 水奏行至汜水，玄佐之柩將發，軍中請備儀仗，瑗不許，又令留器用以俟新使。

translations.literal: As Cou traveled and his memorial reached Si River, Xuanzuo's coffin was about to depart; the army requested full ceremonial escort; Yuan would not permit it, and also ordered the regalia kept to await the new commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu Cou's party reached Si River and Liu Xuanzuo's coffin was about to leave camp, the troops asked for a full ceremonial escort; Lu Yuan refused and ordered the regalia held back until the new commissioner arrived.

sentences.zh: 將士怒。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were angry.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were furious.

sentences.zh: 玄佐之婿及親兵皆被甲，擁玄佐之子士寧釋縗絰，登重榻，自為留後。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo's son-in-law and personal troops all donned armor, supported Xuanzuo's son Liu Shining, who removed mourning hemp and headband, mounted the command couch, and made himself regent.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo's son-in-law and his personal guard donned armor, helped Xuanzuo's son Liu Shining cast off his mourning garb, seated him on the command couch, and proclaimed him acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 執城將曹金岸、浚儀令李邁，曰：「爾皆請吳湊者！」

translations.literal: They seized the garrison commander Cao Jin'an and the magistrate of Junyi Li Mai, saying: "You are all the ones who asked for Wu Cou!"
translations.idiomatic: They seized garrison commander Cao Jin'an and Junyi magistrate Li Mai, crying: "You were the ones who wanted Wu Cou!

sentences.zh: 遂咼之。

translations.literal: They then mutilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Then their noses were cut off.

sentences.zh: 盧瑗逃免。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan fled and escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 士寧以財賞將士，劫孟介以請於朝。

translations.literal: Liu Shining rewarded the officers and soldiers with wealth, seized Meng Jie, and had him petition the court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shining lavished money on the troops, took Meng Jie hostage, and sent him to petition the court on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 上以問宰相，竇參曰：「今汴人指李納以邀制命，不許，將合於納。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers; Dou Can said: "Now the men of Bian are pointing to Li Na to demand an imperial appointment; if it is not granted, they will join with Na."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers. Dou Can said: "The Bianzhou garrison is using Li Na as leverage to demand an imperial commission; refuse them, and they will throw in with Na."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以士寧為宣武節度使。

translations.literal: Day geng-yin; Liu Shining was made military governor of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On the geng-yin day, Liu Shining was appointed military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 士寧疑宋州刺史崔良佐不附己，託言巡撫，至宋州，以都知兵馬使劉逸准代之。

translations.literal: Liu Shining suspected that Songzhou prefect Cui Liangzuo did not adhere to him; on the pretext of an inspection tour he went to Songzhou and replaced him with the commander of all military affairs Liu Yizhun.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting that Songzhou prefect Cui Liangzuo was not loyal to him, Liu Shining went to Songzhou on the pretext of an inspection tour and replaced him with chief military officer Liu Yizhun.

sentences.zh: 逸准，正臣之子也。

translations.literal: Yizhun was the son of Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhun was a son of Liu Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 乙未，貶中書侍郎、同平章事竇參為郴州別駕，貶竇申錦州司戶。

translations.literal: Day yi-wei; Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Councilor Dou Can was demoted to assistant administrator of Chenzhou; Dou Shen was demoted to registrar of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the yi-wei day, Dou Can, vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor, was demoted to assistant administrator of Chenzhou, and Dou Shen to registrar of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞趙憬、兵部侍郎陸贄並為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhao Jing and Vice Minister of War Lu Zhi were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and Lu Zhi, vice minister of war, were both appointed vice directors of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 憬，仁本之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jing was the great-grandson of Renben.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing was a great-grandson of Zhao Renben.

sentences.zh: 張滂請鹽鐵舊簿於班宏，宏不與。

translations.literal: Zhang Pang requested the old salt-and-iron ledgers from Ban Hong; Hong would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang asked Ban Hong for the old salt-and-iron account books; Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 滂與宏共擇巡院官，莫有合者，闕官甚多。

translations.literal: Pang and Hong together selected circuit-inspection officials; none agreed, and many posts were vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Pang and Hong tried jointly to appoint circuit inspectors, but could agree on no one, and many posts remained unfilled.

sentences.zh: 滂言於上曰：「如此，職事必廢，臣罪無所逃。」

translations.literal: Pang said to the emperor: "Thus duties will surely be abandoned, and your servant's guilt will have nowhere to escape."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang told the emperor: "At this rate the office cannot function, and I will have no way to escape blame."

sentences.zh: 丙午，上命宏、滂分掌天下財賦，如大歷故事。

translations.literal: Day bing-wu; the emperor ordered Hong and Pang to divide management of the empire's revenues, as in the Dali precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On the bing-wu day the emperor ordered Hong and Pang to divide control of the empire's finances, following the Dali-era precedent.

sentences.zh: 壬子，吐蕃寇靈州，陷水口支渠，敗營田。

translations.literal: Day ren-zi; Tibetans raided Lingzhou, destroyed the Shuikou branch canal, and defeated the garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: On the ren-zi day the Tibetans raided Lingzhou, breached the Shuikou branch canal, and ravaged the military farms.

sentences.zh: 詔河東、振武救之，遣神策六軍二千戍定遠、懷遠城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong and Zhenwu to rescue; two thousand from the six Shence armies were sent to garrison Dingyuan and Huaiyuan cities.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Hedong and Zhenwu commands to relieve Lingzhou and dispatched two thousand men from the six Shence armies to garrison Dingyuan and Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃乃退。

translations.literal: The Tibetans then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 陸贄請令台省長官各舉其屬，著其名於詔書，異日考其殿最，並以升黜舉者。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi requested that the chiefs of the Censorate and Secretariat each recommend their subordinates, inscribe their names in the edict, and later, when examining their grades of achievement, promote or demote the recommenders together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi proposed that each head of the censorate and secretariat recommend his own subordinates, record their names in the edict, and later, when their performance was graded, reward or punish the recommenders accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰，詔行贄議。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wu-chen; an edict enacted Zhi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the wu-chen day, an edict put Lu Zhi's proposal into effect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，或言於上曰：「諸司所舉皆有情故，或受貨賂，不得實才。」

translations.literal: Before long someone said to the emperor: "All whom the various offices have recommended have personal ties, or accepted bribes, and true talent is not obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone told the emperor: "Every nominee from the ministries was chosen through favoritism or bribery, and none are truly capable."

sentences.zh: 上密諭贄：「自今除改，卿宜自擇，勿任諸司。」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly instructed Zhi: "From now on in appointments and changes, you should choose yourself; do not leave it to the various offices."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor privately told Lu Zhi: "From now on you should make appointments yourself and not leave them to the ministries."

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，其略曰：「國朝五品以上，制敕命之，蓋宰相商議奏可者也。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "In our dynasty, fifth rank and above are appointed by edict and patent—this is what the chief ministers deliberate and memorialize for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi memorialized in reply, in essence: "In our dynasty, officials of the fifth rank and above receive their appointments by imperial edict—matters on which the chief ministers deliberate and then memorialize for approval.

sentences.zh: 六品以下則旨授，蓋吏部銓材署職，詔旨畫聞而不可否者也。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below are appointed by rescript—this is the Ministry of Personnel selecting talent and assigning posts; the edict is noted for information and cannot be refused.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the sixth rank and below are appointed by rescript—the Ministry of Personnel selects talent and assigns posts, and the edict is merely noted for the emperor's information, not subject to refusal.

sentences.zh: 開元中，起居、遺、補、御史等官，猶並列於選曹。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, the offices of diarist, remonstrator, supplementer, and censor were still all listed under the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the Kaiyuan era, diarists, remonstrators, supplementers, and censors were still appointed through the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 其後幸臣專朝，捨僉議而重己權，廢公舉而行私惠，是使周行庶品，苛不出時宰之意，則莫致也。」

translations.literal: Afterward favored ministers monopolized the court, abandoned collective deliberation to exalt their own power, abolished public recommendation to practice private favor—thus making it that throughout the ranks of officials, if they did not strictly accord with the chief minister's intent, none could attain office."
translations.idiomatic: Later, favored ministers dominated the court, set aside collective deliberation to aggrandize their own power, and abandoned open recommendation for private patronage—so that throughout the bureaucracy, no one could gain office unless he pleased the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「宣行以來，才舉十數，議其資望，既不愧於班行，考其行能，又未聞於闕敗。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the edict was promulgated, only a dozen or so have been recommended; considering their qualifications and standing, they are not unworthy among their peers; examining their conduct and ability, nothing has been heard of failure or defect.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Since the edict took effect we have recommended only a dozen or so men; judged by qualification and standing, none disgrace their peers, and in conduct and ability none has yet been found wanting.

sentences.zh: 而議者遽以騰口，上煩聖聰。

translations.literal: Yet critics hastily spread rumors and troubled the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Yet critics have already raised a clamor and troubled Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 道之難行，亦可知矣！

translations.literal: How difficult it is to put the Way into practice may also be known!
translations.idiomatic: How hard it is to put good policy into practice is all too clear!

sentences.zh: 請使所言之人指陳其狀，某人受賄，某舉有情，付之有司，核其虛實。

translations.literal: I ask that those who speak be made to set forth the facts in detail—so-and-so accepted a bribe, so-and-so's recommendation had personal ties—and hand it to the appropriate office to verify truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that accusers be required to specify their charges—who took a bribe, whose nomination was tainted by favoritism—and that the appropriate offices investigate the truth.

sentences.zh: 謬舉者必行其罰，誣善者亦反其辜。

translations.literal: Those who recommended wrongly must suffer punishment; those who slandered the good must also suffer the penalty in return.
translations.idiomatic: Recommenders who erred must be punished, and false accusers must suffer in turn.

sentences.zh: 何必貸其奸贓，不加辯詰，私其公議，不出主名，使無辜見疑，有罪獲縱，枉直同貫，人何賴焉！

translations.literal: Why pardon their wicked bribery, not subject them to examination, privatize public deliberation, and not give the accuser's name—making the innocent be suspected and the guilty go free, crooked and straight treated the same—on what can people rely!
translations.idiomatic: Why shield slander and bribery, refuse cross-examination, and allow anonymous attacks that make the innocent suspect while the guilty go free—when crooked and straight are treated alike, what can the people rely on!

sentences.zh: 又，宰相不過數人，豈能遍諳多士！

translations.literal: Moreover, the chief ministers are only a few in number—how can they be thoroughly acquainted with the many scholars!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, there are only a few chief ministers—how can they know all worthy men in the empire!

sentences.zh: 若令悉命群官，理須展轉詢訪，是則變公舉為私薦，易明揚以暗投，情故必多，為弊益甚。

translations.literal: If all offices were ordered to choose, by principle they would have to inquire through many turns—this would change public recommendation into private nomination, exchange open promotion for secret lobbying; personal ties would surely multiply, and the harm would be still greater.
translations.idiomatic: If every office were ordered to nominate, each would have to canvass through layers of intermediaries—turning public recommendation into private patronage and open selection into back-room lobbying, with favoritism multiplying and the harm far worse.

sentences.zh: 所以承前命官，罕不涉謗。

translations.literal: Therefore those who received appointments under the previous system rarely escaped slander.
translations.idiomatic: That is why officials appointed under the old system were rarely free of scandal.

sentences.zh: 雖則秉鈞不一，或自行情，亦由私訪所親，轉為所賣。

translations.literal: Although those who held the scales of power were not uniform, some acted on their own authority—yet this too came from privately inquiring of those close to them and being sold by them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Even when chief ministers differed and some made appointments on their own, they did so by sounding out their private networks and being steered by them.

sentences.zh: 其弊非遠，聖鑒明知。」

translations.literal: These harms are not distant; Your Sagely Perception clearly knows them."
translations.idiomatic: These abuses are nothing new; Your Majesty sees them clearly."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今之宰相則往日台省長官，今之台省長官乃將來之宰相，但是職名暫異，固非行舉頓殊。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today's chief ministers are yesterday's censorate and secretariat chiefs; today's censorate and secretariat chiefs are tomorrow's chief ministers—only the titles differ for a time; the practice of recommendation is not suddenly different.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Today's chief ministers were yesterday's censorate and secretariat heads; today's censorate and secretariat heads are tomorrow's chief ministers. Only the titles differ for a time—the principle of recommendation does not change overnight.

sentences.zh: 豈有為長官之時則不能舉一二屬吏，居宰相之位則可擇千百具僚。

translations.literal: How can it be that when serving as chief one cannot recommend one or two subordinate officials, yet when occupying the chief minister's post one may choose hundreds and thousands of colleagues?
translations.idiomatic: How can a man be unable to recommend one or two subordinates as a department head, yet claim to choose hundreds of officials as chief minister?

sentences.zh: 物議悠悠，其惑斯甚。

translations.literal: Public discussion is endless; how great is the confusion!
translations.idiomatic: Public rumor runs on endlessly—what confusion this breeds!

sentences.zh: 蓋尊者領其要，卑者任其詳，是以人主擇輔臣，輔臣擇庶長，庶長擇佐僚，將務得人，無易於此。

translations.literal: For the honored grasp the essentials and the humble undertake the details; thus the ruler chooses assisting ministers, assisting ministers choose department chiefs, and department chiefs choose aides—in seeking to obtain the right men, nothing is easier than this.
translations.idiomatic: The superior holds the essentials and the subordinate handles the details; the ruler chooses his ministers, ministers choose department heads, and heads choose their staffs. To secure the right men, no method is simpler.

sentences.zh: 夫求才貴廣，考課貴精。

translations.literal: In seeking talent, breadth is prized; in examination, precision is prized.
translations.idiomatic: In recruiting talent, breadth matters; in evaluation, precision matters.

sentences.zh: 往者則天欲收人心，進用不次，非但人得薦士，亦得自舉其才。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Wu wished to win people's hearts and promoted men out of turn; not only could others recommend scholars, one could also recommend one's own talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu sought to win hearts, she promoted men out of turn—not only could others nominate talent, candidates could nominate themselves.

sentences.zh: 然而課責既嚴，進退皆速，是以當代謂知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。」

translations.literal: Yet because examination and accountability were strict and advancement and dismissal were swift, the age called it discernment in knowing men, and successive reigns relied on the employment of many scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Because evaluation was strict and promotions and dismissals swift, her age was praised for knowing men, and later reigns benefited from the many talents she employed."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「則天舉用之法傷易而得人，陛下慎簡之規太精而失士。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Empress Wu's method of recommendation, though rough and easy, obtained men; Your Majesty's rule of cautious selection is too refined and loses men."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Empress Wu's method was loose but found talent; Your Majesty's cautious selection is so refined that talent is lost."

sentences.zh: 上竟追前詔不行。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end recalled the earlier edict and did not implement it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor revoked the earlier edict and let the policy lapse.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，平盧節度使李納薨。

translations.literal: Day gui-you; Li Na, military governor of Pinglu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the gui-you day, Li Na, military governor of Pinglu, died.

sentences.zh: 軍中推其子師古知留後。

translations.literal: The army promoted his son Shigu to know remaining-affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The army installed his son Li Shigu as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃千餘騎寇涇州，掠田軍千餘人而去。

translations.literal: Sixth month; more than a thousand Tibetan horsemen raided Jingzhou, seized more than a thousand garrison-farm troops, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, over a thousand Tibetan horsemen raided Jingzhou, carried off more than a thousand farm-garrison troops, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使奏：「近日海舶珍異，多就安南市易，欲遣判官就安南收市，乞命中使一人與俱。」

translations.literal: The Lingnan military governor memorialized: "Recently maritime ships' rare goods have mostly gone to Annan for trade; we wish to send a regent official to Annan to purchase them, and ask that one palace envoy be ordered to go together."
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Lingnan reported: "Lately foreign ships have been trading their rare goods chiefly at Annan rather than Guangzhou; we wish to send an aide to Annan to buy them up, and request that a palace envoy accompany him."

sentences.zh: 上欲從之，陸贄上言，以為：「遠國商販，惟利是求，緩之斯來，擾之則去。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to agree; Lu Zhi submitted a statement, holding that: "Merchants from distant states seek profit alone; if treated gently they come, if harassed they leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was inclined to agree, but Lu Zhi objected: "Foreign merchants follow profit alone—treat them gently and they come; harass them and they leave.

sentences.zh: 廣州素為眾舶所湊，今忽改就安南，若非侵刻過深，則必招攜失所，曾不內訟，更蕩上心。

translations.literal: Guangzhou has long been where the many ships gather; now they suddenly shift to Annan—if this is not because exactions are too deep, then it must be that solicitation and guidance have lost their place; they have not even lodged internal complaints, yet already they shake the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou has always been where the fleets congregate; if they suddenly prefer Annan, either our exactions are too harsh or we have failed to win their loyalty. They need not even sue at court to unsettle Your Majesty's mind.

sentences.zh: 況嶺南、安南，莫非王土，中使、外使，悉是王臣，豈必信嶺南而絕安南，重中使以輕外使。

translations.literal: Moreover, Lingnan and Annan are none other than the king's domain; palace envoys and external commissioners are all the king's servants—why must one trust Lingnan and cut off Annan, esteem palace envoys and slight external commissioners?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Lingnan and Annan are alike imperial territory, and palace envoys and frontier commissioners are alike the emperor's servants—why trust one region and spurn the other, or favor a palace envoy over a frontier official?

sentences.zh: 所奏望寢不行。」

translations.literal: The memorial submitted hopes the plan will be laid aside and not carried out."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that this proposal be set aside."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲寅朔，戶部尚書判度支班宏薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day jia-yin; Ban Hong, Minister of Revenue acting as commissioner of revenue, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, Ban Hong, minister of revenue and acting revenue commissioner, died.

sentences.zh: 陸贄請以前湖南觀察使李巽權判度支，上許之。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi requested that the former Hunan observation commissioner Li Xun be made acting commissioner of revenue; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi recommended the former Hunan commissioner Li Xun as acting revenue commissioner, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而復欲用司農少卿裴延齡，贄上言，以為：「今之度支，准平萬貨，刻吝則生患，寬假則容奸。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again wished to employ Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries Pei Yanling; Zhi submitted a statement, holding that: "Today's revenue office balances the myriad goods; if harsh and stingy, trouble arises; if lenient and indulgent, knavery is harbored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor wished to appoint Pei Yanling, vice minister of the Imperial Granaries, instead. Lu Zhi objected: "The revenue office must balance all commodities—too harsh breeds trouble, too lax breeds fraud.

sentences.zh: 延齡誕妄小人，用之交駭物聽。

translations.literal: Yanling is a deceitful, reckless petty man; employ him and at once the public will be shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling is a deceitful schemer; appoint him and you will shock the court and the people alike.

sentences.zh: 尸祿之責，固宜及於微臣。

translations.literal: The liability for holding salary without performing duty should indeed reach this humble minister.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail in my duty, the blame for drawing salary without serving should fall on me alone.

sentences.zh: 知人之明，亦恐傷於聖鑒。」

translations.literal: Discernment in knowing men may also harm Your Sagely Perception."
translations.idiomatic: It may also wound Your Majesty's reputation for discerning men."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 己未，以延齡判度支事。

translations.literal: Day ji-wei; Yanling was made acting commissioner of revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the ji-wei day, Pei Yanling was appointed acting revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河南、北、江、淮、荊、襄、陳、許等四十餘州大水，溺死者二萬餘人，陸贄請遣使賑撫。

translations.literal: More than forty circuits including Henan, Hebei, Jiang-Huai, Jing, Xiang, Chen, and Xu suffered great floods; drowned were more than twenty thousand persons; Lu Zhi requested dispatch of envoys to relieve and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Floods struck more than forty prefectures from Henan and Hebei to the Jiang-Huai, Jing, Xiang, Chen, and Xu regions, drowning over twenty thousand people; Lu Zhi urged the court to send relief envoys.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聞所損殊少，即議優恤，恐生奸欺。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I hear the damage is especially slight; if we at once discuss generous relief, I fear it will breed fraud."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I am told the losses are modest; generous relief now will only invite fraud."

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，其略曰：「流俗之弊，多徇諂諛，揣所悅意則侈其言，度所惡聞則小其事，制備失所，恆病於斯。」

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "The defect of vulgar custom is mostly to follow flattery; guessing what will please, they exaggerate; gauging what will be hated to hear, they minimize the matter—loss of proper preparation constantly afflicts us in this."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi replied in essence: "Vulgar custom favors flattery: tell the ruler what pleases him and the disaster shrinks; tell him what he hates to hear and it vanishes altogether. Misjudging affairs in this way is our chronic disease."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「所費者財用，所收者人心，苛不失人，何憂乏用！」

translations.literal: He also said: "What is spent is wealth; what is gained is people's hearts—if people are not lost, why worry about lack of funds!"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "We spend money to buy loyalty. Lose the people and funds are useless; keep the people and funds will follow."

sentences.zh: 上許為遣使，而曰：「淮西貢賦既闕，不必遣使。」

translations.literal: The emperor agreed to send envoys, but said: "Huai-Xi's tribute and taxes are already lacking; envoys need not be sent there."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed to send envoys but said: "Huai-Xi already owes its tribute; skip it."

sentences.zh: 贄復上奏，以為：「陛下息師含垢，宥彼渠魁，惟茲下人，所宜矜恤。

translations.literal: Zhi again submitted a memorial, holding that: "Your Majesty has ceased hostilities and borne disgrace, pardoning their ringleaders—only these common people below deserve compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi pressed again: "Your Majesty has shown mercy even to rebel leaders; how much more should common folk in disaster receive aid?

sentences.zh: 昔秦、晉仇敵，穆公猶救其饑，況帝王懷柔萬邦，唯德與義，寧人負我，我無負人。」

translations.literal: In former times Qin and Jin were enemies, yet Duke Mu still relieved Jin's famine—how much more should an emperor cherish all realms with virtue and righteousness: better that the people wrong the ruler than that the ruler wrong the people."
translations.idiomatic: When Qin and Jin were bitter foes, Duke Mu still fed Jin in famine. An emperor should rule by virtue: let the people wrong him if they must, but let him never wrong the people."

sentences.zh: 八月，遣中書舍人京兆奚陟等宣撫諸道水災。

translations.literal: Eighth month; dispatched Secretariat Drafting Officer Xi Zhi of Jingzhao and others to proclaim comfort along the circuits for flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Xi Zhi of Jingzhao, a drafting officer of the Secretariat, and others to comfort the flood-stricken circuits.

sentences.zh: 以前青州刺史李師古為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: The former Qingzhou prefect Li Shigu was made military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu, former prefect of Qingzhou, was appointed military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 韋皋攻吐蕃維州，獲其大將論贊熱。

translations.literal: Wei Gao attacked Weizhou in Tibet and captured their great general Lun Zanre.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao attacked the Tibetan stronghold of Weizhou and captured the Tibetan general Lun Zanre.

sentences.zh: 陸贄上言，以邊儲不贍，由措置失當，蓄斂乖宜，其略曰：「所謂措置失當者，戍卒不隸於守臣，守臣不總於元帥。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted a statement, that border stores were insufficient because measures were wrongly set and accumulation wrongly done; in summary: "What is called wrongly set measures is that garrison soldiers are not subordinate to defending officials, and defending officials are not under the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi argued that frontier granaries were empty because policy was wrong and collection mishandled. He wrote: "Garrison troops answer neither local commanders nor the frontier commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至有一城之將，一旅之兵，各降中使監臨，皆承別詔委任。

translations.literal: To the point that for one city's general and one regiment's troops, each had a palace envoy sent down to supervise, all receiving separate edicts of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: A single city might have its own general, a regiment its own troops—each watched by a palace envoy with a separate imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 分鎮亙千里之地，莫相率從。

translations.literal: Divided garrisons stretched across a thousand li, none leading or following another.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons were scattered across a thousand li with no one commander to coordinate them.

sentences.zh: 緣邊列十萬之師，不設謀主。

translations.literal: Along the border were arrayed a hundred thousand troops, yet no strategist was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand men lined the frontier, yet no chief strategist was named.

sentences.zh: 每有寇至，方從中覆，比蒙征發救援，寇已獲勝罷歸。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came, only then was word sought from the center; by the time relief was approved and sent, the raiders had already won and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever enemies struck, the army waited for court approval; by the time relief marched, the raiders were gone.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃之比中國，眾寡不敵，工拙不侔，然而彼攻有餘，我守不足。

translations.literal: Tibet compared with China: numbers unmatched, skill unmatched—yet they attack with surplus and we defend with insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet cannot match China in numbers or craft, yet they attack at will while we barely hold our posts.

sentences.zh: 蓋彼之號令由將，而我之節制在朝，彼之兵眾合併，而我之部分離析故也。

translations.literal: For their orders come from generals, while our command rests at court; their forces are combined, while our parts are divided—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Their orders issue from generals; ours from the capital. Their armies fight as one; ours in fragments—that is why they win.

sentences.zh: 所謂蓄斂乖宜者，陛下頃設就軍、和糴之法以省運，制與人加倍之價以勸農，此令初行，人皆悅慕。

translations.literal: What is called wrongly done accumulation: Your Majesty recently established the methods of army-procurement and harmonized purchase to save transport, fixing double price for men to encourage farming—when this order first ran, all were glad.
translations.idiomatic: Your "wrong accumulation" policy: the army-procurement and harmonized-purchase systems were meant to cut transport costs and pay farmers double—at first everyone rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 而有司競為苟且，專事纖嗇，歲稔則不時斂藏，艱食則抑使收糴。

translations.literal: Yet the offices competed in shiftlessness, specializing in petty stinginess; in good years they did not store in season, in scarce food they forced purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Officials grew lazy and stingy: in good years they failed to buy and store; in famine they forced farmers to sell.

sentences.zh: 遂使豪家、貪吏，反操利權，賤取於人以俟公私之乏。

translations.literal: Thus powerful families and greedy clerks reversed control of profit, buying cheap from people to await public and private want.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families and corrupt clerks seized the trade, buying cheap from peasants to hoard for dearth.

sentences.zh: 又有勢要、近親、羈游之士，委賤糴於軍城，取高價於京邑，又多支絲希絲寧充直。

translations.literal: Also influential persons, close kin, and wandering scholars entrusted cheap purchase at army cities and took high prices at the capital, often paying in inferior silk counted as full value.
translations.idiomatic: Influential men and court connections bought grain cheap at frontier posts and sold it dear in the capital, often paying in shoddy silk at face value.

sentences.zh: 窮邊寒不可衣，鬻無所售。

translations.literal: In the poor border, cold cloth could not be worn and sold nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier the silk was useless—too thin for cold weather and unsellable.

sentences.zh: 上既無信於下，下亦以偽應之，度支物估轉高，軍城谷價轉貴。

translations.literal: Above had no trust in below, below answered with falsity; the revenue office's valuations rose, army-city grain prices rose.
translations.idiomatic: The court lost trust in the frontier; the frontier answered with fraud. Revenue valuations climbed; army grain prices soared.

sentences.zh: 度支以苟售滯貨為功利，軍司以所得加價為羨餘。

translations.literal: The revenue office took quick sale of stagnant goods as profit; army offices took markup as surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The revenue office profited by dumping unwanted goods; army quartermasters by marking up what they received.

sentences.zh: 雖高巡院，轉成囊橐。

translations.literal: Though the circuit-inspection office was lofty, it became a purse.
translations.idiomatic: Even the high circuit-inspection office became a money sack.

sentences.zh: 至有空申簿帳，偽指囷倉，計其數則億萬有餘，考其實則百十不足。」

translations.literal: To the point of empty entries in ledgers, false pointing to granaries—counted in numbers, hundreds of millions and more; examined in fact, not one in ten."
translations.idiomatic: Ledgers were padded and granaries falsely listed—on paper hundreds of millions; in fact not one part in ten."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「舊制以關中用度之多，歲運東方租米，至有斗錢運斗米之言。

translations.literal: He also said: "The old system, because Guanzhong's expenditures were great, yearly transported eastern rent rice—there was even the saying of a coin's cost to transport a coin's rice.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Because Guanzhong consumed so much, the court annually shipped eastern rice—sometimes costing a coin to move a coin's worth of grain.

sentences.zh: 習聞見而不達時宜者，則曰：『國之大事，不計費損，雖知勞煩，不可廢也。』

translations.literal: Those accustomed to what they hear but not grasping the timely said: "The state's great affair does not count cost; though knowing labor and trouble, it cannot be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Conservatives said: "Great affairs ignore expense; transport is burdensome but indispensable."

sentences.zh: 習近利而不防遠患者，則曰：『每至秋成之時，但令畿內和糴，既易集事，又足勸農。』

translations.literal: Those accustomed to near profit but not guarding against distant harm said: "Each autumn harvest, only order the capital region harmonized purchase—easy to gather and enough to encourage farming."
translations.idiomatic: Reformers said: "Each autumn, buy grain around the capital—easy and it helps farmers."

sentences.zh: 臣以兩家之論，互有長短，將制國用，須權重輕。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the two schools' arguments each have strengths and weaknesses; to regulate state use, one must weigh heavy and light.
translations.idiomatic: Both views have merit; fiscal policy must balance grain against coin.

sentences.zh: 食不足而財有餘，則弛於積財而務實倉廩；

translations.literal: When food is insufficient yet wealth surplus, relax hoarding wealth and strive to fill granaries;
translations.idiomatic: When grain is scarce but money plentiful, spend coin to fill granaries;

sentences.zh: 食有餘而財不足，則緩於積食而嗇用貨泉。

translations.literal: when food is surplus yet wealth insufficient, slow hoarding grain and be sparing with currency.
translations.idiomatic: when grain is plentiful but money tight, hoard grain and conserve coin.

sentences.zh: 近歲關輔屢豐，公儲委積，足給數年；

translations.literal: In recent years Guanzhong has repeatedly been abundant; public stores piled up, enough for several years;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong has had rich harvests; public stores could feed the capital for years;

sentences.zh: 今夏江、淮水潦，米貴加倍，人多流庸。

translations.literal: this summer Jiang-Huai flooded; rice doubled in price; many became wandering laborers.
translations.idiomatic: this summer the Jiang-Huai flooded; rice doubled; multitudes became refugees.

sentences.zh: 關輔以谷賤傷農，宜加價以糴而無錢；

translations.literal: Guanzhong, because grain was cheap, hurt farmers—should raise price to purchase but had no money;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong farmers were hurt by cheap grain—the court should buy high but lacked funds;

sentences.zh: 江、淮以谷貴人困，宜減價以糶而無米。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai, because grain was dear, people were distressed—should lower price to sell out but had no rice.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai people were crushed by dear grain—the court should sell low but had no grain to sell.

sentences.zh: 而又運彼所乏，益此所餘，斯所謂習見聞而不達時宜者也。

translations.literal: Yet again transporting what they lacked to add to what we had in surplus—this is what is called accustomed to hearing but not grasping the timely.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court still shipped grain from surplus regions to needy ones—the very folly of blind custom.

sentences.zh: 今江、淮斗米直百五十錢，運至東渭橋，僦直又約二百，米糙且陳，尤為京邑所賤。

translations.literal: Now Jiang-Huai rice per dou is worth 150 cash; transported to East Wei Bridge, hire costs another 200; the rice is coarse and stale, especially despised in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai rice now costs 150 cash per dou; freight to East Wei Bridge adds 200; the grain arrives coarse and stale, despised in the capital.

sentences.zh: 據市司月估，斗糶三十七錢。

translations.literal: According to the market office's monthly estimate, each dou sold for 37 cash.
translations.idiomatic: The market office valued it at only 37 cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 耗其九而存其一，餒彼人而傷此農，制事若斯，可謂深失矣！

translations.literal: Nine parts lost and one retained, starving those people and hurting these farmers—if policy is thus, it may be called deeply wrong!
translations.idiomatic: Nine parts in ten were wasted, starving the Jiang-Huai and hurting Guanzhong farmers—a profound blunder.

sentences.zh: 頃者每年自江、湖、淮、浙運米百一十萬斛，至河陰留四十萬斛，貯河陰倉，至陝州又留三十萬斛，貯太原倉，餘四十萬斛輸東渭橋。

translations.literal: Recently each year from Jiang, lakes, Huai, and Zhe 1,100,000 hu of rice were transported; at Heyin 400,000 hu were left in Heyin granary; at Shaanzhou another 300,000 hu in Taiyuan granary; the remaining 400,000 hu went to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Each year 1.1 million hu were shipped from the southeast: 400,000 stored at Heyin, 300,000 at Taiyuan in Shaanzhou, 400,000 to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 今河陰、太原倉見米猶有三百二十餘萬斛，京兆諸縣斗米不過直錢七十，請令來年江、淮止運三十萬斛至河陰，河陰、陝州以次運至東渭橋，其江、淮所停運米八十萬斛，委轉運使每斗取八十錢於水災州縣糶之，以救貧乏，計得錢六十四萬緡，減僦直六十九萬緡。

translations.literal: Now Heyin and Taiyuan granaries still have more than 3,200,000 hu on hand; in Jingzhao counties rice per dou is not more than 70 cash. Request that next year Jiang-Huai transport only 300,000 hu to Heyin, Heyin and Shaanzhou in turn to East Wei Bridge; the 800,000 hu of Jiang-Huai rice stopped from transport, entrust the transport commissioner to take 80 cash per dou in flood counties to sell out and relieve the poor—counting 640,000 strings of cash, reducing hire costs 690,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: Heyin and Taiyuan still hold 3.2 million hu; Jingzhao rice sells for 70 cash. Next year ship only 300,000 hu from Jiang-Huai to Heyin, then forward to East Wei Bridge; sell the withheld 800,000 hu in flood districts at 80 cash per dou for relief—640,000 strings gained, 690,000 strings saved in freight.

sentences.zh: 請令戶部先以二十萬緡付京兆，令糴入以補渭橋倉之缺數，斗用百錢以利農人。

translations.literal: Request the Ministry of Revenue first pay 200,000 strings to Jingzhao to purchase grain to fill Wei Bridge granary's shortage, 100 cash per dou to benefit farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Advance 200,000 strings to Jingzhao to buy grain at 100 cash per dou for Wei Bridge and aid farmers.

sentences.zh: 以一百二萬六千緡付邊鎮，使糴十萬人一年之糧，餘十萬四千緡以充來年和糴之價。

translations.literal: Pay 1,026,000 strings to border commands to purchase a year's grain for 100,000 men; the remaining 104,000 strings for next year's harmonized purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Send 1,026,000 strings to the frontier for a year's grain for 100,000 troops; reserve 104,000 for next year's purchases.

sentences.zh: 其江、淮米錢、僦直並委轉運使折市綾、絹、絁、綿，以輸上都，償先貸戶部錢。」

translations.literal: The Jiang-Huai rice money and hire costs all entrust the transport commissioner to exchange for silk, gauze, and cotton to send to the capital and repay the advance from the Ministry of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Let the transport commissioner trade Jiang-Huai proceeds into silk and cloth for the capital and repay the treasury advance."

sentences.zh: 九月，詔西北邊貴糴以實倉儲，邊備浸充。

translations.literal: Ninth month; an edict ordered the northwest frontier to purchase grain dear to fill granaries; border preparations gradually filled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the court ordered the northwest to buy grain at premium prices to fill frontier granaries.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, first day ren-zi; there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the eleventh month, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃、雲南日益相猜，每雲南兵至境上，吐蕃輒亦發兵，聲言相應，實為之備。

translations.literal: Tibet and Yunnan daily grew more suspicious of each other; whenever Yunnan troops reached the border, Tibet also sent troops, claiming mutual response but in fact guarding against them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet and Yunnan grew mutually suspicious: whenever Yunnan marched to the border, Tibet mobilized too, claiming support but actually guarding against Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，韋皋復遺雲南王書，欲與共襲吐蕃，驅之雲嶺之外，悉平吐蕃城堡，獨與雲南築大城於境上，置戍相保，永同一家。

translations.literal: Day xin-you; Wei Gao again sent a letter to the King of Yunnan, wishing jointly to attack Tibet, drive them beyond Cloud Ridge, level all Tibetan fortresses, and with Yunnan alone build a great city on the border, set garrisons to guard each other, forever one family.
translations.idiomatic: On the xin-you day Wei Gao again wrote the King of Nanzhao, proposing a joint strike to drive Tibet beyond the Cloud Ridge, destroy its forts, and build a great border city where Tang and Nanzhao would garrison together as one household.

sentences.zh: 右庶子姜公輔久不遷官，詣陸贄求遷，贄密語之曰：「聞竇相屢奏擬，上不允，有怒公之言。」

translations.literal: Right Court Gentleman Jiang Gongfu long went without promotion; he went to Lu Zhi seeking advancement; Zhi told him secretly: "I hear Chief Minister Dou repeatedly submitted nominations; the emperor did not approve; there are words of anger against you."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu, a right court gentleman, had long gone without promotion and asked Lu Zhi for help. Zhi whispered: "Dou Can kept nominating you; the emperor refused—he is angry at you."

sentences.zh: 公輔懼，請為道士。

translations.literal: Gongfu was afraid and requested to become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Gongfu asked to become a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，公輔不敢洩贄語，以聞參言為對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Gongfu dared not reveal Zhi's words and answered with what he had heard of Can's remarks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Gongfu dared not repeat Zhi's warning and blamed Dou Can instead.

sentences.zh: 上怒參歸怨於君。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Can shifted blame onto the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged that Dou Can had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 己巳，貶公輔為吉州別駕，又遣中使責參。

translations.literal: Day ji-si; Gongfu was demoted to assistant administrator of Jizhou; also sent a palace envoy to rebuke Can.
translations.idiomatic: On the ji-si day Jiang Gongfu was demoted to Jizhou and a palace envoy was sent to rebuke Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 庚午，山南西道節度使嚴震奏敗吐蕃於芳州及黑水堡。

translations.literal: Day geng-wu; Yan Zhen, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, memorialized defeating Tibet at Fangzhou and Heishui Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On the geng-wu day Yan Zhen of Shannan West reported victories over Tibet at Fangzhou and Heishui Fort.

sentences.zh: 初，李納以棣州蛤蟲朵有鹽利，城而據之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Na because Hachongduo in Dezhou had salt profits, walled it and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Na had seized Hachongduo in Dezhou for its salt works and fortified it.

sentences.zh: 又戍德州之南三汊城，以通田緒之路。

translations.literal: Also garrisoned Sancha City south of Dezhou to open the road to Tian Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He also garrisoned Sancha City south of Dezhou to keep contact with Tian Xu.

sentences.zh: 及李師古襲位，王武俊以其年少，輕之，是月，引兵屯德、棣，將取蛤蟲朵及三汊城。

translations.literal: When Li Shigu succeeded, Wang Wujun, because he was young, despised him; this month he led troops to camp at De and Di, intending to take Hachongduo and Sancha City.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shigu succeeded, Wang Wujun despised his youth and this month marched on De and Di to seize Hachongduo and Sancha City.

sentences.zh: 師古遣趙鎬將兵拒之。

translations.literal: Shigu sent Zhao Hao to lead troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu sent Zhao Hao to resist.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使諭止之，武俊乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to order him to stop; Wujun then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to halt him; Wujun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，劉怦薨，劉濟在莫州，其母弟澭在父側，以父命召濟而以軍府授之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Zong died, Liu Ji was at Mozhou; his younger brother by the same mother, Yong, was at their father's side; by the father's order he summoned Ji and gave him the military government.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong died, Liu Ji was at Mozhou; his half-brother Liu Yong at their father's side summoned Ji by paternal order and handed him the command.

sentences.zh: 濟以澭為瀛州刺史，許它日代己。

translations.literal: Ji made Yong prefect of Yingzhou, promising to replace himself another day.
translations.idiomatic: Ji made Yong prefect of Yingzhou, promising Yong would succeed him one day.

sentences.zh: 既而濟用其子為副大使，澭怨之，擅通表朝廷，遣兵千人防秋。

translations.literal: Afterward Ji used his son as deputy commissioner; Yong resented it, on his own sent memorials to court, and dispatched a thousand troops for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ji appointed his son deputy commissioner; Yong resented this, memorialized the court on his own, and sent a thousand men for autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 濟怒，發兵擊澭，破之。

translations.literal: Ji was angry, sent troops to attack Yong, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji attacked Yong and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 左神策大將軍柏良器，募才勇之士以易販鬻者，監軍竇文場惡之。

translations.literal: Left Shence Grand General Bai Liangqi recruited brave men to replace traders; army supervisor Dou Wenchang hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Liangqi, grand general of the Left Shence Army, replaced merchants in the ranks with brave recruits; supervisor Dou Wenchang resented it.

sentences.zh: 會良器妻族飲醉，寓宿宮捨。

translations.literal: It happened that Liangqi's wife's kin drank drunk and lodged in a palace lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liangqi's in-laws got drunk and slept in a palace lodge.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，良器坐左遷右領軍。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day bing-xu; Liangqi was demoted for the offense to Right Army Leader.
translations.idiomatic: On the bing-xu day of the twelfth month Liangqi was demoted to Right Army Leader.

sentences.zh: 自是宦官始專軍政。

translations.literal: From this eunuchs began to monopolize military government.
translations.idiomatic: From this time eunuchs began to dominate military affairs.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝九貞元九年（

translations.literal: The Divine Martial and Sagely Literary Emperor Dezong, ninth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of the Tang, ninth year of the Zhenyuan era (

sentences.zh: 癸酉，公元七九三年）

translations.literal: gui-you, CE 793)
translations.idiomatic: gui-you, 793 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，初稅茶。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day gui-mao; tea was taxed for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the gui-mao day of the first month, the tea tax was introduced.

sentences.zh: 凡州、縣產茶及茶山外要路，皆估其直，什稅一，從鹽鐵使張滂之請也。

translations.literal: All prefectures and counties producing tea and key roads outside tea mountains were assessed value; one-tenth taxed—following Salt and Iron Commissioner Zhang Pang's request.
translations.idiomatic: Every tea-producing prefecture and major route was assessed; a ten-percent tax was levied at Zhang Pang's request.

sentences.zh: 滂奏：「去歲水災減稅，用度不足，請稅茶以足之。

translations.literal: Pang memorialized: "Last year's flood disaster reduced taxes; expenditures are insufficient; request tea tax to make up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang argued: "Last year's floods cut revenue; tax tea to fill the gap.

sentences.zh: 自明年以往，稅茶之錢，令所在別貯，俟有水旱，以代民田稅。」

translations.literal: From next year onward, tea-tax money shall be stored separately where collected; when flood or drought, use in place of people's field tax."
translations.idiomatic: Tea revenue would be stored locally and, in future droughts or floods, substitute for field taxes."

sentences.zh: 自是歲收茶稅錢四十萬緡，未嘗以救水旱也。

translations.literal: From this each year 400,000 strings of tea-tax money were collected, yet never used to relieve flood or drought.
translations.idiomatic: Yet thereafter 400,000 strings a year were collected and never used for disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 滂又奏：「奸人銷錢為銅器以求贏，請悉禁銅器。

translations.literal: Pang also memorialized: "Wicked men melt coin to make copper vessels for profit; request all copper vessels forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: “Pang also asked to ban copper vessels made by melting coinage.

sentences.zh: 銅山聽人開採，無得私賣。

translations.literal: Copper mountains may be mined by people; private sale is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Copper mines were opened to licensed mining; private sale was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，以義武留後張升雲為節度使。

translations.literal: Second month, day jia-yin; Zhang Shengyun, regent of Yiwu, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the jia-yin day of the second month Zhang Shengyun, acting governor of Yiwu, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 初，鹽州既陷，塞外無復保障。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yanzhou fell, beyond the passes there was no further protection.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhou fell, the outer defenses were gone.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃常阻絕靈武，侵擾鄜坊。

translations.literal: Tibet often blocked Lingwu and raided Bin and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet repeatedly cut Lingwu and raided Bin and Fang.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔發兵三萬五千人城鹽州，又詔涇原、山南、劍南各發兵深入吐蕃以分其勢，城之二旬而畢。

translations.literal: Day xin-you; an edict mobilized 35,000 men to wall Yanzhou; also ordered Jingyuan, Shannan, and Jiannan each to send troops deep into Tibet to divide their strength; the wall was finished in twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: On the xin-you day 35,000 men were ordered to rebuild Yanzhou; Jingyuan, Shannan, and Jiannan were to raid Tibet to divide its forces; the work took twenty days.

sentences.zh: 命鹽州節度使杜彥光戍之，朔方都虞候楊朝晟戍木波堡，由是靈、武銀、夏、河西獲安。

translations.literal: Ordered Yanzhou military governor Du Yanguang to garrison it; Shuofang chief adjutant Yang Chaosheng to garrison Mubo Fort—thereby Ling, Wu, Yin, Xia, and Hexi were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanguang garrisoned Yanzhou and Yang Chaosheng Mubo Fort, securing Lingzhou, Wu, Yin, Xia, and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 上使人諭陸贄，以「要重之事，勿對趙憬陳論，當密封手疏以聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to instruct Lu Zhi that "on weighty matters, do not discuss with Zhao Jing in the open; seal a handwritten memorial and report."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Lu Zhi not to discuss weighty matters openly with Zhao Jing but to submit sealed memorials."

sentences.zh: 又「苗粲以父晉卿往年攝政，嘗有不臣之言，諸子皆與古帝王同名，今不欲明行斥逐，兄弟亦各除外官，勿使近屯兵之地。」

translations.literal: Also: "Miao Can, because his father Jinqing once held regency, had disloyal words; his sons all share ancient emperors' names; now the emperor does not wish openly to expel them—the brothers also each take outside posts; do not let them near garrisoned troops."
translations.idiomatic: He also said Miao Can's father had spoken treasonously while regent and that Can's sons bore imperial names; they should be quietly posted far from armies."

sentences.zh: 又「卿清慎太過，諸道饋遺，一皆拒絕，恐事情不通，如鞭靴之類，受亦無傷。」

translations.literal: Also: "Your scrupulousness is excessive; gifts from all circuits you entirely refuse—I fear affairs will not get through; things like whips and boots, receiving does no harm."
translations.idiomatic: He also said Lu Zhi was too austere to accept gifts—even boots and whips might be accepted without harm."

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，其略曰：「昨臣所奏，惟趙憬得聞，陛下已至勞神，委曲防護。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial, in summary: "Yesterday my memorial was heard only by Zhao Jing; Your Majesty has already troubled yourself, elaborately protecting me.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi replied: "Only Zhao Jing heard my last memorial, yet Your Majesty already labors to shield me in secret.

sentences.zh: 是於心膂之內，尚有形跡之拘，跡同事殊，鮮克以濟。

translations.literal: This is within the heart and vitals yet still having traces of constraint; traces the same but affairs different—rarely can it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Even among your closest ministers I am constrained—same forms, different trust—such secrecy rarely succeeds.

sentences.zh: 恐爽無私之德，且傷不吝之明。」

translations.literal: I fear it will offend impartial virtue and also wound unstinting clarity."
translations.idiomatic: It will seem partial and wound your reputation for openness."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「爵人必於朝，刑人必於市，惟恐眾之不睹，事之不彰。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ennobling men must be in court, punishing men in the market—only fearing the masses do not see and affairs are not manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He said honors must be public and punishments visible to all.

sentences.zh: 君上行之無愧心，兆庶聽之無疑議，受賞安之無怍色，當刑居之無怨言，此聖王所以宣明典章，與天下公共者也。

translations.literal: The ruler acts without guilty heart; the myriad hear without doubtful debate; receiving reward they are at ease without shame; facing punishment they dwell without complaint—this is why sage kings proclaim statutes and share them with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only then do rewards bring no shame and punishments no rumor—how sage kings make law common property.

sentences.zh: 凡是譖訴之事，多非信實之言，利於中傷，懼於公辯。

translations.literal: Generally matters of slander and accusation are mostly not truthful words, profitable for striking the center, fearful of public debate.
translations.idiomatic: Slander thrives on secrecy and fears open debate.

sentences.zh: 或雲歲月已久，不可究尋；

translations.literal: Some say the years are already long and cannot be investigated;
translations.idiomatic: Some say the matter is too old to investigate;

sentences.zh: 或雲事體有妨，須為隱忍；

translations.literal: some say the affair has obstacles and must be quietly endured;
translations.idiomatic: some that it is too delicate to air;

sentences.zh: 或雲惡跡未露，宜假它事為名；

translations.literal: some say the wicked tracks are not yet exposed and it is fitting to borrow another affair as name;
translations.idiomatic: some that guilt is unproven and another pretext should be used;

sentences.zh: 或雲但棄其人，何必明言責辱。

translations.literal: some say only abandon the man, why must one openly speak reproach and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: some that the man should simply be removed without stating the charge.

sentences.zh: 詞皆近於情理，意實苑於矯誣，傷善售奸，莫斯為甚！

translations.literal: The words all approach reasonableness, but the intent truly gardens in forced falsehood—injuring the good and selling wickedness, nothing exceeds this!
translations.idiomatic: Their words sound reasonable, but the aim is deceit—to harm the innocent and shield the guilty. Nothing is worse.

sentences.zh: 若晉卿父子實有大罪，則當公議典憲；

translations.literal: If Jinqing father and son truly have great crimes, then public deliberation and statutory punishment should apply;
translations.idiomatic: If the Jinqings are truly guilty, let the law judge them openly;

sentences.zh: 若被誣枉，豈令陰受播遷。

translations.literal: if falsely accused, how can they be made to suffer secret banishment.
translations.idiomatic: if they are slandered, they must not be quietly exiled.

sentences.zh: 夫聽訟辨讒，必求情辨跡，情見跡著，辭服理窮，然後加刑罰焉，是以下無冤人，上無謬聽。」

translations.literal: In hearing lawsuits and distinguishing slander, one must seek facts and distinguish traces; when feeling appears and traces are clear, words submit and reason is exhausted—only then apply punishment; thus below there are no wronged men, above no mistaken hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Justice requires facts and evidence. Only when guilt is clear should punishment fall—then the people are not wronged and the throne not misled."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「監臨受賄，盈尺有刑，至於士吏之微，尚當嚴禁，矧居風化之首，反可通行！

translations.literal: He also said: "Supervisors accepting bribes: a foot's measure has punishment; as for the slightness of clerks and officials, it should still be strictly forbidden—how much more the head of transforming custom, yet it may pass!
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Bribery by overseers is a capital crime even for minor clerks—how then may the chief minister of morals accept gifts?

sentences.zh: 賄道一開，展轉滋甚，鞭靴不已，必及金玉。

translations.literal: Once the bribery road opens, it turns and grows; whips and boots unceasing, must reach gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Open the door to gifts and they escalate from boots and whips to gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 目見可欲，何能自窒於心！

translations.literal: The eye sees what is desirable—how can the heart block itself!
translations.idiomatic: Who can resist what the eye desires?

sentences.zh: 已與交私，何能中絕其意！

translations.literal: Already in private dealings—how can one cut off their intent midway!
translations.idiomatic: Once private ties are formed, how can favor be refused?

sentences.zh: 是以涓流不絕，溪壑成災矣。」

translations.literal: Thus trickling streams unceasing, ravines and gullies become disaster."
translations.idiomatic: A trickle becomes a torrent and ravines overflow."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「若有所受，有所卻，則遇卻者疑乎見拒而不通矣；

translations.literal: He also said: "If some are accepted and some refused, then those refused will suspect being rejected and not communicate;
translations.idiomatic: If you accept some gifts and refuse others, those refused will think themselves shunned;

sentences.zh: 若俱辭不受，則咸知不受者乃其常理，復何嫌阻之有乎！」

translations.literal: if all are declined, then all know that declining is the constant rule—what suspicion or obstruction remains!"
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse all alike, everyone knows refusal is your rule and no one is singled out."

sentences.zh: 初，竇參惡左司郎中李巽，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dou Can hated Left Department Bureau Director Li Xun and sent him out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can had banished Li Xun from the Left Department to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 及參貶郴州，巽為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: When Can was demoted to Chenzhou, Xun was Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can was demoted to Chenzhou, Li Xun was Hunan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汴州節度使劉士寧遺參絹五十匹，巽奏參交結籓鎮。

translations.literal: Bianzhou military governor Liu Shining sent Can fifty bolts of silk; Xun memorialized that Can was in league with frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shining of Bianzhou sent Dou Can fifty bolts of silk; Li Xun reported that Can was colluding with regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，欲殺參，陸贄以為參罪不至死，上乃止，既而復遣中使謂贄曰：「參交結中外，其意難測，社稷事重，卿速進文書處分。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and wished to kill Can; Lu Zhi held that Can's crime did not reach death; the emperor then stopped; shortly after again sent a palace envoy telling Zhi: "Can is in league inside and outside; his intent is hard to fathom; the altars of state are weighty—quickly advance documents to dispose."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted Dou Can executed; Lu Zhi argued the crime did not warrant death and the emperor relented—then an envoy told Zhi: "Can conspires far and wide; act at once."

sentences.zh: 贄上言：「參朝廷大臣，誅之不可無名。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted: "Can is a court great minister; to execute him there must be no lack of name.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said: "Dou Can is a chief minister; he cannot be killed without clear cause.

sentences.zh: 昔劉晏之死，罪不明白，至今眾議為之憤邑，叛臣得以為辭。

translations.literal: In former times Liu Yan's death—the crime was not clear; to this day public debate is indignant for him; rebel ministers could use it as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan was executed without clear guilt, the realm was outraged and rebels used it as propaganda.

sentences.zh: 參貪縱之罪，天下共知；

translations.literal: Can's crimes of greed and indulgence—the realm jointly knows;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can's greed is notorious;

sentences.zh: 至於潛懷異圖，事跡曖昧。

translations.literal: as for secretly harboring other designs, the traces are dim.
translations.idiomatic: but treason is unproven.

sentences.zh: 若不推鞫，遽加重辟，駭動不細。

translations.literal: If without investigation one hastily adds heavy punishment, the shock is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: To execute him without trial would shock the empire.

sentences.zh: 竇參於臣無分，陛下所知，豈欲營救其人，蓋惜典刑不濫。」

translations.literal: Dou Can has no tie with your servant; Your Majesty knows—how would I wish to rescue the man? I cover the statutes lest they be abused."
translations.idiomatic: I do not seek to save Dou Can for friendship's sake, Your Majesty, but to keep punishment from excess."

sentences.zh: 三月，更貶參驩州司馬，男女皆配流。

translations.literal: Third month; Can was further demoted to military adjutant of Huanzhou; men and women all sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Dou Can was demoted to Huanzhou and his family exiled.

sentences.zh: 上又命理其親黨，贄奏：「罪有首從，法有重輕，參既蒙宥，親黨亦應末減。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered punishment of his kin; Zhi memorialized: "Crime has principals and followers, law has heavy and light; since Can has received mercy, kin also should be reduced at the margin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to punish Can's clan; Lu Zhi said kin should receive lighter sentences now that Can was spared.

sentences.zh: 況參得罪之初，私黨並已連坐，人心久定，請更不問。」

translations.literal: Moreover at the beginning of Can's offense, private cliques were already implicated; people's hearts long settled—request no further inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: His partisans were already punished when he fell; the matter is settled—do not reopen it."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上又欲籍其家貲，贄曰：「在法，反逆者盡沒其財，贓污者止征所犯。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to confiscate his household property; Zhi said: "In law, rebels have all property confiscated; embezzlers only levy what was stolen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to seize Can's estate; Lu Zhi cited law: only rebels lose all property; embezzlers pay restitution.

sentences.zh: 皆須結正施刑，然後收籍。

translations.literal: All must conclude guilt and apply punishment, then collect registers.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt must be proved before confiscation.

sentences.zh: 今罪法未詳，陛下已存惠貸，若簿錄其家，恐以財傷義。」

translations.literal: Now crime and law are not detailed; Your Majesty already intends merciful loan—if ledgers of the household are recorded, I fear wealth will injure righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The charges are unclear and Your Majesty already shows mercy—forfeiture would sacrifice justice to greed.

sentences.zh: 時宦官左右恨參尤深，謗毀不已。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs left and right hated Can especially deeply and slandered without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs kept slandering Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 參未至驩州，竟賜死於路。

translations.literal: Can had not yet reached Huanzhou when he was granted death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Huanzhou, Dou Can was ordered to die on the road.

sentences.zh: 竇申杖殺，貨財、奴婢悉傳送京師。

translations.literal: Dou Shen was beaten to death; goods and slaves were all sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Shen was beaten to death; his property and slaves were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 海州團練使張升璘，升雲之弟，李納之婿也。

translations.literal: Haizhou training commissioner Zhang Shenglian was Shengyun's younger brother and Li Na's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenglian of Haizhou was Zhang Shengyun's brother and Li Na's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 以父大祥歸於定州，嘗於公座罵王武俊，武俊奏之。

translations.literal: Because his father's great mourning he returned to Dingzhou; once at public seat he cursed Wang Wujun; Wujun memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he returned to Dingzhou and publicly cursed Wang Wujun, who reported him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑，詔削其官，遣中使杖而囚之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day ding-chou; an edict stripped his office and sent a palace envoy to cane and imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the ding-chou day of the fourth month, he was stripped of rank, caned, and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 定州富庶，武俊常欲之，因是遣兵襲取義豐，掠安喜、無極萬餘口，徙之德、棣。

translations.literal: Dingzhou was rich; Wujun had long wanted it; on this pretext he sent troops to seize Yifeng, plundered more than ten thousand persons of Anxi and Wuji, and moved them to De and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun had long coveted rich Dingzhou; he seized Yifeng and carried off more than ten thousand people from Anxi and Wuji to De and Di.

sentences.zh: 升雲閉城自守，屢遣使謝之，乃止。

translations.literal: Shengyun closed the city and held defense, repeatedly sent envoys to apologize, and only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shengyun shut the city and apologized until Wujun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上命李師古毀三汊城，師古奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Li Shigu to destroy Sancha City; Shigu obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Shigu to demolish Sancha City, and he obeyed.

sentences.zh: 然常招聚亡命，有得罪於朝廷者，皆撫而用之。

translations.literal: Yet he constantly gathered fugitives; those who had offended the court he comforted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he sheltered fugitives and outlaws from the court.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲辰，以中書侍郎趙憬為門下侍郎、同平章事，義成節度使賈耽為在右僕射，右丞盧邁守本官，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jia-chen; Vice Director Zhao Jing was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Councilor; Yicheng military governor Jia Dan was made Left and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Right Vice Director Lu Mai kept his post—all Co-Equal Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On the jia-chen day of the fifth month Zhao Jing became chancellor of the Chancellery, Jia Dan vice director of state affairs, and Lu Mai remained right vice director—all as co-equal grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 邁，翰之族子也。

translations.literal: Mai was a clansman of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mai was a kinsman of Lu Han.

sentences.zh: 憬疑陸贄恃恩，欲專大政，排己置之門下，多稱疾不豫事，由是與贄有隙。

translations.literal: Jing suspected Lu Zhi relied on favor and wished to monopolize great government, pushed himself aside to place him in the Chancellery, often claimed illness and did not attend affairs—thereby he and Zhi had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing suspected Lu Zhi of monopolizing power, kept himself aloof claiming illness, and fell out with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 陸贄上奏論備邊六失，以為「措置乖方，課責虧度，財匱於兵眾，力分於將多，怨生於不均，機失於遙制。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted a memorial discussing six failures in border defense, holding that "measures wrongly set, assessments deficient, wealth exhausted on troops, strength divided among many generals, resentment born from inequality, opportunity lost through remote control.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi memorialized on six border failures: bad organization, lax discipline, wasted funds, divided command, unfair pay, and delayed orders from the capital.

sentences.zh: 「關東戍卒，不習土風，身苦邊荒，心畏戎虜。

translations.literal: " Guandong garrison soldiers do not learn local custom; body suffers border waste, heart fears barbarian foes.
translations.idiomatic: " Guandong troops know neither frontier climate nor enemy ways;

sentences.zh: 國家資奉若驕子，姑息如倩人。

translations.literal: The state supports them like spoiled children, indulges like hired men.
translations.idiomatic: the court pampers them like spoiled children.

sentences.zh: 屈指計歸，張頤待哺；

translations.literal: Counting fingers for return, opening mouths awaiting feed;
translations.idiomatic: They count the days until rotation and live on rations;

sentences.zh: 或利王師之敗，乘擾攘而東潰；

translations.literal: some profit from the royal army's defeat, ride disturbance to flee east;
translations.idiomatic: some hope for defeat so they can flee east;

sentences.zh: 或拔棄城鎮，搖遠近之心。

translations.literal: some abandon garrison towns, shaking hearts near and far.
translations.idiomatic: some abandon posts and unsettle the frontier.

sentences.zh: 豈惟無益，實亦有損。

translations.literal: How is it only without benefit—it actually also has harm.
translations.idiomatic: They do more harm than good.

sentences.zh: 復有犯刑謫徙者，既是無良之類，且加懷土之情，思亂幸災，又甚戍卒。

translations.literal: Also those who violated law and were banished—being already the unworthy sort, and adding love of native soil, thinking of disorder and hoping for disaster, they are even more than garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled criminals are worse still—restless men who welcome chaos.
