sentences.zh: 可謂措置乖方矣。

translations.literal: It may be called wrongly set measures.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first failure: wrong organization.

sentences.zh: 自頃權移於下，柄失於朝，將之號令既鮮克行之於軍，國之典常又不能施之於將，務相遵養，苟度歲時。

translations.literal: Recently power shifted below, the handle lost at court; generals' orders are rarely enforced in the army, the state's constants cannot be applied to generals—all mutually indulging, barely passing the years.
translations.idiomatic: Generals no longer command; the court no longer disciplines them—all merely marking time.

sentences.zh: 欲賞一有功，翻慮無功者反仄；

translations.literal: Wishing to reward one with merit, one fears the meritless will be uneasy;
translations.idiomatic: Reward one man and others grow jealous;

sentences.zh: 欲罰一有罪，復慮同惡者憂虞。

translations.literal: wishing to punish one with crime, again fears the like-wicked will worry.
translations.idiomatic: punish one and accomplices fear.

sentences.zh: 罪以隱忍而不彰，功以嫌疑而不賞，姑息之道，乃至於斯。

translations.literal: Crime is concealed and not manifest; merit is suspected and not rewarded—the way of indulgence reaches to this.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes are hidden and merit suspected—indulgence gone too far.

sentences.zh: 故使忘身效節者獲誚於等夷，率眾先登者取怨於士卒，僨軍蹙國者不懷於愧畏，緩救失期者自以為智能。

translations.literal: Thus those who forget body and show loyalty are mocked by equals; those who lead masses and advance first draw troops' resentment; those who lose armies and press the state feel no shame; those who delay rescue past term think themselves clever.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal are mocked, the brave resented, the incompetent unashamed, and the tardy call themselves wise.

sentences.zh: 此義士所以痛心，勇夫所體。

translations.literal: This is why men of righteousness grieve and brave men weep.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous men grieve and warriors despair.

sentences.zh: 可謂課責虧度矣。

translations.literal: It may be called deficient assessment.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second failure: lax discipline.

sentences.zh: 虜每入寇，將帥遞相推倚，無敢誰何。

translations.literal: Whenever the barbarians enter to raid, generals pass blame in turn, none daring to confront.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders strike, generals blame one another and dare not fight.

sentences.zh: 虛張賊勢上聞，則曰兵少不敵。

translations.literal: Falsely inflating bandit power reported above, then saying troops few and not a match.
translations.idiomatic: They exaggerate enemy strength and plead insufficient troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷莫之省察，唯務征發益師，無裨備御之功，重增供億之弊。

translations.literal: The court does not examine; only strives to levy and increase troops—no help to defense, heavily adding supply burdens.
translations.idiomatic: The court only sends more men, helping neither defense nor finance.

sentences.zh: 閭井日耗，徵求日繁，以編戶傾家、破產之資，兼有司榷鹽、稅酒之利，總其所入，歲以事邊。

translations.literal: Hamlets daily waste, levies daily numerous—using registered households' ruined family and broken estate resources, together with monopoly salt and wine taxes of the offices; totaling their intake, yearly it serves the border.
translations.idiomatic: Villages are ruined by endless levies, salt and wine monopolies included—all to feed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 可謂財匱於兵眾矣。

translations.literal: It may be called wealth exhausted on troops.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third failure: wasted funds.

sentences.zh: 「吐蕃舉國勝兵之徒，才當中國十數大郡而已，動則中國懼其眾而不敢抗，靜則中國憚其強而不敢侵，厥理何哉？

translations.literal: " Tibet's whole state of victorious soldiers amounts only to a dozen or so great commanderies of China—yet when they move, China fears their multitude and dares not resist; when quiet, China dreads their strength and dares not invade—what is the principle?
translations.idiomatic: " Tibet's entire army equals only a dozen Chinese prefectures—yet we fear them. Why?

sentences.zh: 良以中國之節制多門，蕃丑之統帥專一故也。

translations.literal: Truly because China's controls are many gates and the barbarian chieftain's command is unified.
translations.idiomatic: Because our command is fragmented and theirs is unified.

sentences.zh: 夫統帥專一，則人心不分，號令不貳，進退可齊，疾徐中意，機會靡愆，氣勢自壯。

translations.literal: When command is unified, hearts do not divide, orders are not twofold, advance and retreat can be aligned, fast and slow accord with intent, opportunity without error, spirit naturally strong.
translations.idiomatic: Unified command unifies hearts and orders; opportunity is seized and spirit strong.

sentences.zh: 斯乃以少為眾，以弱為強者也。

translations.literal: This is taking few as many, weak as strong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus few become many and weak become strong.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶之間，控御西北兩蕃，唯朔方、河西、隴右三節度。

translations.literal: Between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, controlling northwest two barbarians relied only on Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou three commands.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan and Tianbao only three commands faced the northwest.

sentences.zh: 中興以來，未遑外討，抗兩蕃者亦朔方、涇原、隴右、河東四節度而已。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, not yet able to campaign abroad, those resisting the two barbarians were also only Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong four commands.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration only four commands bore the burden.

sentences.zh: 自頃分朔方之地，建牙擁節者凡三使焉，其餘鎮軍，數且四十，皆承特詔委寄，各降中貴監臨，人得抗衡，莫相稟屬。

translations.literal: Recently dividing Shuofang's territory, those who set teeth and held banners were three commissioners; the remaining garrison armies, numbering nearly forty, all received special edict entrustment, each had eunuch supervisors—men could balance one another, none obeying another.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang was split among three commissioners and nearly forty independent armies, each with its own eunuch overseer—none obeying another.

sentences.zh: 每俟邊書告急，方令計會用兵，既無軍法下臨，惟以客禮相待。

translations.literal: Each time border reports cried urgent, only then were troops counted for use; with no military law descending, only guest ritual was exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came, they met as equals without military law.

sentences.zh: 夫兵，以氣勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；

translations.literal: Soldiers take spirit and momentum as function; spirit gathered then flourishing, scattered then dissipated;
translations.idiomatic: Armies live by morale; gathered it flourishes, scattered it fades.

sentences.zh: 勢合則威，析則弱。

translations.literal: momentum combined then awe-inspiring, divided then weak.
translations.idiomatic: United they are formidable, divided weak.

sentences.zh: 今之邊備，勢弱氣消，可謂力分於將多矣。

translations.literal: Today's border defense: momentum weak, spirit dissipated—it may be called strength divided among many generals.
translations.idiomatic: Today's frontier is weak and divided—the fourth failure.

sentences.zh: 「理戎之要，在於練核優劣之科以為衣食等級之制，使能者企及，否者息心，雖有薄厚之殊而無觖望之釁。

translations.literal: " The essentials of ordering the barbarians lie in refining grades of merit and demerit for food and clothing ranks, making the able aspire and the unable rest heart—though there are thick and thin differences, no resentment of inequality.
translations.idiomatic: " Pay and rank should reflect merit so the able strive and the rest accept their lot.

sentences.zh: 今窮邊之地，長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷之餘，終年勤苦之劇，然衣糧所給，唯止當身，例為妻子所分，常有凍餒之色。

translations.literal: Now in poor border lands, long-garrisoned troops are all remnants of a hundred battles wounded, year-long toil severe; yet clothing and grain given reach only the body, customarily divided by wives and children, often with freezing and hunger color.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier veterans who fought for years are paid barely enough to feed themselves while their families freeze.

sentences.zh: 而關東戍卒，怯於應敵，懈於服勞，衣糧所頒，厚逾數等。

translations.literal: Yet Guandong garrison soldiers, cowardly in facing foes, slack in labor—clothing and grain issued exceed several grades.
translations.idiomatic: Guandong troops, cowards in battle, receive several times more.

sentences.zh: 又有素非禁旅，本是邊軍，將校詭為媚詞，因請遙隸神策，不離舊所，唯改虛名，其於廩賜之饒，遂有三倍之益。

translations.literal: Also some originally not of the imperial guard, originally border troops—generals with flattery asked to be remotely attached to Shence, not leaving old place, only changing empty name; their granary stipends' abundance then had triple benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Some border units were nominally transferred to the Shence Army without moving yet tripled their pay.

sentences.zh: 夫事業未異而給養有殊，苛未忘懷，孰能無慍！

translations.literal: Affairs not different yet support different—if harshness is not forgotten, who can be without anger!
translations.idiomatic: Same service, unequal pay—who would not resent it?

sentences.zh: 可謂怨生於不均矣。

translations.literal: It may be called resentment born from inequality.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth failure: unfair pay.

sentences.zh: 「凡欲選任將帥，必先考察行能，可者遣之，不可者退之，疑者不使，使者不疑，故將在軍，君命有所不受。

translations.literal: " Generally in wishing to select and appoint generals, one must first examine conduct and ability; the fit send them, the unfit dismiss them; the doubtful do not employ, envoys do not doubt—thus generals in the army, the ruler's command has what is not received.
translations.idiomatic: " Choose generals by merit and trust them in the field.

sentences.zh: 自頃邊軍去就，裁斷多出宸衷，選置戎臣，先求易制，多其部以分其力，輕其任以弱其心，遂令爽於軍情亦聽命，乖於事宜亦聽命。

translations.literal: Recently border armies' coming and going, decisions mostly came from the imperial breast; selecting border officials, first seeking easy control; increasing their departments to divide their strength, lightening their tasks to weaken their hearts—thus even contrary to army feeling they obey, contrary to affairs they obey.
translations.idiomatic: The court picks pliant generals, splits their commands, and micromanages from afar.

sentences.zh: 戎虜馳突，迅如風飆，馹書上聞，旬月方報。

translations.literal: Barbarians charge and raid swift as wind; relay reports upward, half a month before reply.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders strike like wind; court replies take a month.

sentences.zh: 守土者以兵寡不敢抗敵，分鎮者以無詔不肯出師，賊既縱掠退歸，此乃陳功告捷。

translations.literal: Defenders with few troops dare not resist; divided commanders without edict will not march; bandits having plundered and withdrawn, then this is reporting merit and victory.
translations.idiomatic: Local defenders dare not fight; neighboring commands wait for edicts; raiders leave and generals claim victory.

sentences.zh: 其敗喪則減百而為一，其捃獲則張百而成千。

translations.literal: Their defeat and loss is reduced from a hundred to one; their captures are inflated from one to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Defeats are minimized; booty exaggerated.

sentences.zh: 將帥既幸於總制在朝，不憂罪累，陛下又以為大權由己，不究事情。

translations.literal: Generals are fortunate that overall control is at court, not worrying guilt; Your Majesty also thinks great power is yours and does not examine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Generals know the court will not blame them; the emperor does not investigate.

sentences.zh: 可謂機失於遙制矣。

translations.literal: It may be called opportunity lost through remote control.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth failure: remote control.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂宜罷諸道將士防秋之制，令本道但供衣糧，募戍卒願留及蕃、漢子弟以給之。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly proposes: abolish all circuits' soldiers' autumn-defense system; let each circuit only supply clothing and grain, recruit garrison soldiers willing to remain and barbarian and Han youths to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ending autumn rotations, local pay, local recruitment, and expanded frontier farms.

sentences.zh: 又多開屯田，官為收糴，寇至則人自為戰，時至則家自力農，與夫倏來忽往者，豈可同等而論哉！

translations.literal: Also open more military farms; the government purchases grain; when bandits come people fight on their own, when season comes families farm on their own—how can this be equal to those who come suddenly and go suddenly!
translations.idiomatic: Farmers would fight when raiders came and farm in peace otherwise—unlike rotating outsiders.

sentences.zh: 又宜擇文武能臣為隴右、朔方、河東三元帥，分統緣邊諸節度使，有非要者，隨所便近而並之。

translations.literal: Also select civil and military able ministers as three commanders-in-chief for Longyou, Shuofang, and Hedong, dividing command of border military governors; where unnecessary, merge according to convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He urged three frontier marshals to unify scattered commands.

sentences.zh: 然後減奸濫虛浮之費以豐財，定衣糧等級之制以和眾，弘委任之道以宣其用，懸賞罰之典以考其成。

translations.literal: Then reduce corrupt and floating expenses to enrich wealth, fix clothing and grain grades to harmonize the masses, broaden entrustment to declare their use, suspend reward and punishment codes to examine their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Cut waste, standardize pay, delegate authority, and enforce rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 如是，則戎狄威懷，疆場寧謐矣。」

translations.literal: If thus, then barbarians will be awed and soothed, and the frontier will be tranquil."
translations.idiomatic: Then the frontier would be secure.

sentences.zh: 上雖不能盡從，心甚重之。

translations.literal: Though the emperor could not entirely follow, in heart he greatly valued it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not adopt all of it but greatly respected the memorial.

sentences.zh: 韋皋遣大將董面力等將兵出西山，破吐蕃之眾，拔堡柵五十餘。

translations.literal: Wei Gao sent great general Dong Mianli and others to lead troops out West Mountain, defeated Tibetan forces, and captured more than fifty forts and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao's general Dong Mianli raided from the west and took fifty Tibetan forts.

sentences.zh: 丙午，門下侍郎、同平章事董晉罷為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Day bing-wu; Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Councilor Dong Jin was removed to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the bing-wu day Dong Jin was demoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 雲南王異牟尋遣使者三輩，一出戎州，一出黔州，一出安南，各繼生金、丹砂詣韋皋。

translations.literal: The King of Yunnan Yimouxun sent three missions of envoys—one out of Rongzhou, one Qianzhou, one Annan—each continuing to present native gold and cinnabar to Wei Gao.
translations.idiomatic: King Yimouxun of Nanzhao sent three missions with gold and cinnabar to Wei Gao.

sentences.zh: 金以示堅，丹砂以示赤心，三分皋所與書為信，皆達成都。

translations.literal: Gold to show firmness, cinnabar to show red heart; three parts of Gao's letters as trust—all reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gold meant constancy, cinnabar loyalty; they carried three copies of Gao's letters to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋上表請棄吐蕃歸唐，並遺皋帛書，自稱唐故雲南王孫、吐蕃贊普義弟日東王。

translations.literal: Yimouxun submitted a memorial requesting to abandon Tibet and return to Tang, also sending Gao silk letters, styling himself Tang's former King of Yunnan's grandson, Tibet's sworn younger brother, King of the Eastern Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun asked to defect from Tibet to Tang, calling himself grandson of the old King of Yunnan and sworn brother to Tibet's tsenpo.

sentences.zh: 皋遣其使者詣長安，並上表賀。

translations.literal: Gao sent his envoys to Chang'an and also submitted a memorial of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent the envoys to Chang'an with a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 上賜異牟尋詔書，令皋遣使慰撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yimouxun an edict ordering Gao to send envoys to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict to Yimouxun and ordered Gao to send envoys to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 賈耽、陸贄、趙憬、盧邁為相，百官白事，更讓不言。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, Lu Zhi, Zhao Jing, and Lu Mai were chief ministers; officials reporting affairs yielded and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: With Jia Dan, Lu Zhi, Zhao Jing, and Lu Mai as chief ministers, officials deferred to one another and rarely spoke up.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，奏請依至德故事，宰相迭秉筆以處政事，旬日一易；

translations.literal: Seventh month, autumn; memorialized requesting according to Zhide precedent that chief ministers take turns holding the brush to handle government affairs, changing every ten days;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they asked to revive the Zhide practice of rotating chief ministers every ten days;

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: an edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 其後日一易之。

translations.literal: Afterward it changed every day.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it became daily rotation.

sentences.zh: 劍南、西山諸羌女王湯立志、哥鄰王董臥庭、白狗王羅陀忽、弱水王董辟和、南水王薛莫庭、悉董王湯悉贊、清遠王蘇唐磨、咄霸王董邈蓬及逋租王，先皆役屬吐蕃，至是各帥眾內附。

translations.literal: Qiang queens and kings of Jiannan West Mountain—Queen Tang Lizhi, King Dong Woting of Geling, King Luotuo Hu of the White Dog, King Dong Pihe of Weak Water, King Xue Moting of South Water, King Tang Xizan of Xidong, King Su Tangmo of Qingyuan, King Dong Miaopeng of the Duoba, and kings who fled rent—all had formerly served Tibet; now each led masses to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang and tribal leaders of the western mountains who had served Tibet now led their people to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 韋皋處之於維、保、霸州，給以耕牛種糧。

translations.literal: Wei Gao settled them in Wei, Bao, and Ba prefectures, giving plow oxen and seed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao resettled them in Wei, Bao, and Ba and gave them oxen and seed.

sentences.zh: 立志、陀忽、辟和入朝，皆拜官，厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: Lizhi, Tuohu, and Pihe entered court, all were appointed officials, richly rewarded and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhi, Tuohu, and Pihe came to court, received offices and rich gifts, and returned.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，戶部侍郎裴延齡奏：「自判度支以來，檢責諸州欠負錢八百餘萬緡，收諸州抽貫錢三百萬緡，呈樣物三十餘萬緡，請別置欠負耗剩季庫以掌之，染練物則別置月庫以掌。」

translations.literal: Day gui-mao; Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yanling memorialized: "Since acting as revenue commissioner, I have examined and verified owing money from various prefectures of more than 8,000,000 strings, collected various prefectures' withheld money 3,000,000 strings, presented sample goods more than 300,000 strings—request separately establishing a quarterly granary for owing and surplus to manage it, and for dyed and refined goods a monthly granary."
translations.idiomatic: On the gui-mao day Pei Yanling claimed to have found 8 million strings in prefectural debts, 3 million in withheld funds, and 300,000 in sample goods, and asked for new storehouses.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 欠負皆貧人無可償，徒存其數者，抽貫錢給用隨盡，呈樣、染練皆左藏正物。

translations.literal: The owing were all poor with nothing to repay—only numbers kept on the books; withheld money for use was quickly spent; samples and dyed goods were all proper items of the left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The debts were uncollectible from the poor; withheld funds were spent; the goods were already in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 延齡徙置別庫，虛張名數以惑上。

translations.literal: Yanling moved them to separate granaries, falsely inflating names and numbers to delude the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling merely moved existing stock to new ledgers and inflated the figures.

sentences.zh: 上信之，以為能富國而寵之，於實無所增也，虛費吏人簿書而已。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him, thought he could enrich the state and favored him; in fact nothing was added, only wasting clerks' ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Pei Yanling enriched the state, though nothing was actually gained.

sentences.zh: 京城西污濕地生蘆葦數畝，延齡奏稱長安、咸陽有陂澤數百頃，可牧廄馬。

translations.literal: West of the capital, wet ground produced several mu of reeds; Yanling memorialized saying Chang'an and Xianyang had marshes of several hundred qing where stud horses could be pastured.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed hundreds of qing of marsh near Chang'an could pasture horses though only a few mu of reeds existed.

sentences.zh: 上使有司閱視，無之，亦不罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent officials to inspect; there were none, yet he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors found nothing, yet Pei Yanling went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 左補闕權德輿上奏，以為：「延齡取常賦支用未盡者充羨餘以為己功。

translations.literal: Left Supplementation Remonstrator Quan Deyu submitted, holding that: "Yanling takes regular levies not yet spent as surplus for his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu said Yanling counted unspent regular revenue as his own surplus.

sentences.zh: 縣官先所市物，再給其直，用充別貯。

translations.literal: What the officials earlier purchased, he paid again and used to fill separate storage.
translations.idiomatic: He repaid the treasury for goods already bought and called it new savings.

sentences.zh: 邊軍自今春以來並不支糧。

translations.literal: Border armies since this spring have all received no grain.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops had received no grain since spring.

sentences.zh: 陛下必以延齡孤貞獨立，時人醜正流言，何不遣信臣覆視，究其本末，明行賞罰。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must think Yanling stands alone and pure while people of the time hate the upright and spread rumors—why not send a trusted minister to re-inspect, trace root and branch, and clearly apply reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to investigate Yanling and punish him if guilty.

sentences.zh: 今群情眾口喧於朝市，豈京城士庶皆為朋黨邪！

translations.literal: Now public feeling and many mouths clamor in court and market—are all capital gentry and commoners party members!
translations.idiomatic: The whole capital was clamoring—is everyone a conspirator?

sentences.zh: 陛下亦宜稍回聖慮而察之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty also should slightly turn sagely thought and examine it."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should reconsider.

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，太尉、中書令、西平忠武王李晟薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day geng-xu; Grand Preceptor, Palace Secretary, and Faithful Martial King of Xiping Li Sheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On the geng-xu day of the eighth month Li Sheng, Prince of Xiping, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，韋皋遣其節度巡官崔佐時繼詔書詣雲南，並自為皋書答之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jia-zi; Wei Gao sent his circuit inspection officer Cui Zuoshi following the edict to Yunnan, and himself wrote Gao's reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wei Gao sent Cui Zuoshi to Nanzhao with an imperial edict and his own letter.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙酉，上祀圓丘，赦天下。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yi-you; the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the yi-you day of the eleventh month the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 劉士寧既為宣武節度使，諸將多不服。

translations.literal: After Liu Shining became Xuanwu military governor, many generals did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Many generals refused to obey Liu Shining.

sentences.zh: 士寧淫亂殘忍，出畋輒數日不返，軍中苦之。

translations.literal: Shining was licentious, disorderly, and cruel; going out to hunt he often did not return for several days—the army suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel and licentious, hunting for days while the army suffered.

sentences.zh: 都知兵馬使李萬榮得眾心，士寧疑之，奪其兵權，令攝汴州事。

translations.literal: Chief military officer Li Wanrong won the masses' hearts; Shining suspected him, stripped his military authority, and ordered him to act for Bianzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanrong was popular; Shining stripped his command and made him act for Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，士寧帥眾二萬畋於外野。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yi-mao; Shining led twenty thousand masses to hunt in the outer wilds.
translations.idiomatic: On the yi-mao day Shining took twenty thousand men hunting.

sentences.zh: 萬榮晨入使府，召所留親兵千餘人，詐之曰：「敕征大夫入朝，以吾掌留務，汝輩人賜錢三十緡。」

translations.literal: Wanrong entered the commissionerate at dawn, summoned the thousand-odd personal troops left behind, deceived them saying: "An edict summons the commissioner to court; I hold remaining affairs—you each receive thirty strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong seized the office at dawn, told the garrison an edict had recalled Shining and paid each man thirty strings.

sentences.zh: 眾皆拜。

translations.literal: All bowed.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed in acceptance.

sentences.zh: 又諭外營兵，皆聽命。

translations.literal: Also instructed the outer-camp soldiers—all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The outer camps obeyed as well.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵閉城門，使馳白士寧曰：「敕征大夫，宜速就路，少或遷延，當傳首以獻。」

translations.literal: Then divided troops to close city gates, sent a rider to tell Shining: "An edict summons the commissioner—you should quickly take the road; if you delay even slightly, your head will be presented."
translations.idiomatic: He closed the gates and told Shining to leave at once or lose his head.

sentences.zh: 士寧知眾不為用，以五百騎逃歸京師，比至東都，所餘僕妾而已。

translations.literal: Shining knew the masses would not serve him; with five hundred horsemen fled to the capital; by the time he reached the eastern capital only remaining servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Shining fled to the capital with five hundred horsemen, arriving with only servants.

sentences.zh: 至京師，敕歸第行喪，禁其出入。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, an edict ordered him to return to his residence to observe mourning and forbade his going out.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was confined to his house in mourning.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使吳少誠聞變，發兵屯郾城，遣使問故，且請戰。

translations.literal: Huai-Xi military governor Wu Shaoqian heard of the change, sent troops to camp at Yancheng, dispatched envoys to ask the reason and also requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoqian of Huai-Xi mobilized at Yancheng and challenged Wanrong.

sentences.zh: 萬榮以言戲之，少誠慚而退。

translations.literal: Wanrong jested in reply; Shaoqian withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong mocked him and Shaoqian withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上聞萬榮逐士寧，使問陸贄，贄上奏，以為今軍州已定，宜且遣朝臣宣勞，徐察事情，冀免差失，其略曰：「今士寧見逐，雖是眾情，萬榮典軍，且非朝旨。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Wanrong had expelled Shining and asked Lu Zhi; Zhi submitted, holding that now army and prefectures were settled—should for the time dispatch court ministers to proclaim comfort, slowly observe affairs, hoping to avoid error; in summary: "Now Shining is expelled—though it is the masses' feeling, Wanrong commands the army and it is not yet court order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Lu Zhi, who warned that Wanrong acted without imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 此安危強弱之機也，願陛下審之慎之。」

translations.literal: This is the occasion of safety and danger, strength and weakness—may Your Majesty examine and be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: This was a critical moment requiring caution.

sentences.zh: 上復使謂贄：「若更淹遲，恐於事非便。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent to tell Zhi: "If further delayed, I fear it will not be convenient for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said delay was dangerous.

sentences.zh: 今議除一親王充節度使，且令萬榮知留後，其制即從內出。」

translations.literal: Now the plan is to appoint one imperial prince as military governor, and for the time let Wanrong know remaining affairs—the appointment will come from within."
translations.idiomatic: He would appoint an imperial prince and let Wanrong act as regent.

sentences.zh: 贄復上奏，其略曰：「臣雖服戎角力諒匪克堪，而經武伐謀或有所見。

translations.literal: Zhi again submitted, in summary: "Your servant though wearing military horns and strength surely cannot bear it, yet in military classics and stratagem perhaps there is some view.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi replied that he was no general but saw the danger.

sentences.zh: 夫制置之安危由勢，付授之濟否由才。

translations.literal: Disposition's safety and danger depend on circumstance; entrustment's success or failure depend on talent.
translations.idiomatic: Security depends on circumstance, success on talent.

sentences.zh: 勢如器焉，惟在所置，置之夷地則平。

translations.literal: Circumstance is like a vessel—only in where it is placed; place it on level ground and it is level.
translations.idiomatic: Like a vessel, placement determines stability.

sentences.zh: 才如負焉，唯在所授，授逾其力則踣。

translations.literal: Talent is like a burden—only in what is entrusted; entrust beyond its strength and it stumbles.
translations.idiomatic: Like a load, exceeding capacity brings collapse.

sentences.zh: 萬榮今所陳奏，頗涉張皇，但露徼求之情，殊無退讓之禮，據茲鄙躁，殊異循良。

translations.literal: What Wanrong now memorializes quite touches exaggeration—only exposing eager-seeking feeling, utterly lacking yielding ritual; judging this vulgar impatience, it is very different from following the good.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong's memorials were boastful and grasping, not modest.

sentences.zh: 又聞本是滑人，偏厚當州將士，與之相得，才止三千，諸營之兵已甚懷怨。

translations.literal: Also heard he is originally from Hua, partial and thick to that prefecture's officers and soldiers—getting along with them, force only three thousand; the various camps' soldiers already greatly resent.
translations.idiomatic: A native of Hua, he favored only three thousand local troops while alienating the rest.

sentences.zh: 據此頗僻，亦非將材，若得志驕盈，不悖則敗，悖則犯上，敗則僨軍。」

translations.literal: Judging this quite perverse, he is also not general material; if he gets his wish and grows arrogant, if not rebellious then defeated, rebellious then offending superiors, defeated then ruining the army."
translations.idiomatic: He was no true general; success would make him arrogant and ruin the army.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「苟邀則不順，苟允則不誠，君臣之間，勢必嫌阻。

translations.literal: Also said: "If invited then not compliant, if granted then not sincere—between ruler and minister, suspicion and obstruction are inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Granting his wish would breed insincerity and suspicion.

sentences.zh: 與其圖之於滋蔓，不若絕之於萌芽。」

translations.literal: Better to cut it in the sprout than figure it in spreading growth."
translations.idiomatic: Better to stop him early than when entrenched.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「為國之道，以義訓人，將教事君，先令順長。」

translations.literal: Also said: "The way of governing a state is to instruct people with righteousness; in teaching subjects to serve the ruler, first order obedience to superiors."
translations.idiomatic: The state must teach obedience before rewarding rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「方鎮之臣，事多專制，欲加之罪，誰則無辭！

translations.literal: Also said: "Frontier commanders' affairs are mostly autocratic; wishing to add crime—who lacks words!
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders are hard to punish—any excuse will serve.

sentences.zh: 若使傾奪之徒便得代居其任，利之所在，人各有心，此源潛滋，禍必難救。

translations.literal: If those who overthrow and seize may at once replace them in office, where profit lies each has his heart—this source secretly grows, disaster surely hard to save.
translations.idiomatic: If usurpers are rewarded, others will seize power for profit.

sentences.zh: 非獨長亂之道，亦關謀逆之端。」

translations.literal: Not only the way of long disorder—it also touches the beginning of plotting rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: It would encourage rebellion, not merely disorder.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「昨逐士寧，起於倉卒，諸郡守將固非連謀，一城師人亦未協志。

translations.literal: Also said: "Yesterday expelling Shining arose in haste; various prefecture defenders were certainly not in joint plot; one city's officers and men also did not unite in will.
translations.idiomatic: The coup was hasty; garrisons were not united in conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 各計度於成敗之勢，回遑於逆順之名，安肯捐軀與之同惡！」

translations.literal: Each calculated success and failure's momentum, hesitated over rebellious and compliant names—how willing to abandon body and share wickedness with him!"
translations.idiomatic: Each man weighed odds and would not die for Wanrong.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下但選文武群臣一人命為節度，仍降優詔，慰勞本軍。

translations.literal: Also said: "Your Majesty need only choose one civil or military minister and appoint him military governor, still lower a gracious edict comforting the original army.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a proper commissioner and comfort the army with an edict.

sentences.zh: 獎萬榮以撫定之功，別加寵任，褒將士以輯睦之義，厚賜資裝，揆其大情，理必寧息。

translations.literal: Reward Wanrong with the merit of pacification, separately add favor and trust; praise officers and soldiers with the meaning of harmony, richly bestow resources—gauging their great feeling, reason surely brings calm.
translations.idiomatic: Reward Wanrong for pacifying the mutiny but give command to a court appointee.

sentences.zh: 萬榮縱欲跋扈，勢何能為！」

translations.literal: Wanrong even if he wishes to be overbearing—what power can he have!"
translations.idiomatic: Then Wanrong could not become a warlord.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「倘後事有愆素，臣請受敗橈之罪。」

translations.literal: Also said: "If later affairs have constant fault, your servant requests to receive the crime of defeat and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi offered to accept punishment if wrong.

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以通王諶為宣武節度大使，以萬榮為留後。

translations.literal: Day ren-xu; Prince of Tong Chen was made Xuanwu military governor ambassador; Wanrong was made regent.
translations.idiomatic: On the ren-xu day Prince Chen was named Xuanwu governor and Wanrong regent.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，納故駙馬都尉郭曖女為廣陵王淳妃。

translations.literal: Day ding-mao; the former Princess Consort of the imperial son-in-law Guo En's daughter was taken in as consort of Prince of Guangling Chun.
translations.idiomatic: On the ding-mao day Guo En's daughter became consort to Prince Chun of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 淳，太子之長子。

translations.literal: Chun was the crown prince's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was the crown prince's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 妃母，即昇平公主也。

translations.literal: The consort's mother was Princess Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Princess Shengping.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝九貞元十年（

translations.literal: The Divine Martial and Sagely Literary Emperor Dezong, tenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of the Tang, tenth year of the Zhenyuan era (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元七九四年）

translations.literal: jia-xu, CE 794)
translations.idiomatic: jia-xu, 794 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，劍南、西山羌、蠻二萬餘戶來降。

translations.literal: Spring, first month; more than twenty thousand households of Jiannan West Mountain Qiang and barbarians came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In spring more than twenty thousand Qiang and tribal households submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔加韋皋押近界羌、蠻及西山八國使。

translations.literal: An edict added to Wei Gao the post of commissioner for nearby Qiang, barbarians, and the eight western kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao was made commissioner over nearby tribes and the eight western kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 崔佐時至雲南所都羊苴咩城，吐蕃使者數百人先在其國，雲南王異牟尋尚不欲吐蕃知之，令佐時衣牂柯服而入。

translations.literal: When Cui Zuoshi reached Yunnan's capital Yangjumie City, several hundred Tibetan envoys were already in that country; King Yimouxun still did not wish Tibet to know and ordered Zuoshi to enter wearing Zangke dress.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanzhao's capital, Tibetan envoys were present; Yimouxun wanted Cui Zuoshi to dress like a tribal envoy.

sentences.zh: 佐時不可，曰：「我大唐使者，豈得衣小夷之服！」

translations.literal: Zuoshi would not, saying: "I am an envoy of great Tang—how can I wear petty barbarian dress!
translations.idiomatic: Cui refused: "I am a Tang envoy and will not dress as a barbarian!"

sentences.zh: 異牟尋不得已，夜迎之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun had no choice and received him by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun received him secretly at night.

sentences.zh: 佐時大宣詔書，異牟尋恐懼，顧左右失色。

translations.literal: Zuoshi greatly proclaimed the edict; Yimouxun was afraid, looked left and right, faces changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was read, Yimouxun was terrified.

sentences.zh: 業已歸唐，乃歔欷流涕，俯伏受詔。

translations.literal: Already having returned to Tang, then he sighed and wept, prostrated to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Having chosen Tang, he wept and accepted the edict prostrate.

sentences.zh: 鄭回密見佐時教之，故佐時盡得其情，因勸異牟尋悉斬吐蕃使者，去吐蕃所立之號，獻其金印，復南詔舊名。

translations.literal: Zheng Hui secretly saw Zuoshi and taught him; therefore Zuoshi fully got their situation, and urged Yimouxun to execute all Tibetan envoys, remove Tibet's established title, present their gold seal, and restore Nanzhao's old name.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hui briefed Cui Zuoshi, who urged Yimouxun to kill the Tibetan envoys and restore the name Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋皆從之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun agreed to all.

sentences.zh: 仍刻金契以獻。

translations.literal: Still carved a gold covenant to present.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a gold covenant of alliance.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋帥其子尋夢湊等與佐時盟於點蒼山神祠。

translations.literal: Yimouxun led his son Xun Mengchen and others to ally with Zuoshi at Cangshan Mountain spirit shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He allied with Cui at the shrine on Cangshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃與回鶻爭北庭，大戰，死傷頗眾，徵兵萬人於雲南。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tibet and the Uyghurs contended for Beiting, fought greatly, dead and wounded quite many; levied ten thousand troops from Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet and the Uyghurs fought over Beiting and demanded ten thousand troops from Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋辭以國小，請發三千人，吐蕃少之。

translations.literal: Yimouxun declined because the state was small, requested to send three thousand; Tibet thought it few.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun offered only three thousand; Tibet demanded more.

sentences.zh: 益至五千，乃許之。

translations.literal: When it reached five thousand, then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At five thousand Tibet agreed.

sentences.zh: 異牟尋遣五千人前行，自將數萬人踵其後，晝夜兼行，襲擊吐蕃，戰於神川，大破之，取橋等十六城，虜其五王，降其眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Yimouxun sent five thousand men ahead, himself led several tens of thousands following, day and night double march, raided Tibet, fought at Shen River, greatly defeated them, took sixteen cities including Qiao, captured five kings, reduced their masses more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five thousand ahead, then attacked with tens of thousands at Shen River, took sixteen cities and captured five kings.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，遣使來獻捷。

translations.literal: Day wu-xu; sent envoys to present victory.
translations.idiomatic: On the wu-xu day he reported victory to Tang.

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史劉澭為兄濟所逼，請西扞隴坻，遂將部兵千五百人、男女萬餘口詣京師，號令嚴整，在道無一人敢取人雞犬者。

translations.literal: Yingzhou prefect Liu Yong, pressed by his elder brother Ji, requested to defend Longqi westward; then led fifteen hundred troops and more than ten thousand men and women to the capital—commands strict and orderly, on the road not one dared take people's chickens and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong fled his brother Liu Ji to court with fifteen hundred troops and ten thousand civilians, harming no property on the march.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，二月，丙午，以為秦州刺史、隴右經略軍使，理普潤。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this; second month, day bing-wu; made Qinzhou prefect and Longyou frontier commissioner, administering at Purun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him Qinzhou prefect and Longyou commissioner at Purun.

sentences.zh: 軍中不擊柝，不設音樂。

translations.literal: In the army they did not strike watch-clappers, did not set music.
translations.idiomatic: His camp struck no night watches and held no music.

sentences.zh: 士卒病者，澭親視之，死者哭之。

translations.literal: Where soldiers were ill, Yong personally viewed them; where dead, he wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed the sick and mourned the dead.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，義成節度使李融薨。

translations.literal: Day yi-chou; Yicheng military governor Li Rong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yi-chou day Li Rong of Yicheng died.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以華州刺史李復為義成節度使。

translations.literal: Day ding-mao; Huazhou prefect Li Fu was made Yicheng military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the ding-mao day Li Fu became governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 復，齊物之子也。

translations.literal: Fu was Qiwu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu was a son of Li Qiwu.

sentences.zh: 復辟河南尉洛陽盧坦為判官。

translations.literal: Fu recruited Henan Wei Luoyang Commandant Lu Tan as regent.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Lu Tan of Luoyang as his aide.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍數侵軍政，坦每據理以拒之。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Xue Yingzhen repeatedly encroached on military government; Tan each time resisted on principle.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Xue Yingzhen meddled; Lu Tan resisted on principle.

sentences.zh: 盈珍常曰：「盧侍御所言公，我固不違也。」

translations.literal: Yingzhen often said: "What Remonstrator Lu says is public—I certainly will not violate it."
translations.idiomatic: Xue said Lu Tan was always right and he would not oppose him."

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使程懷直入朝，厚賜遣歸。

translations.literal: Heng-Hai military governor Cheng Huairu entered court, was richly rewarded and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Huairu of Heng-Hai came to court, was rewarded, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，宣武軍亂，留後李萬榮討平之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day geng-wu; Xuanwu army mutinied; regent Li Wanrong suppressed and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the geng-wu day, Xuanwu mutinied and Wanrong crushed it.

sentences.zh: 先是，宣武親兵三百人素驕橫，萬榮惡之，遣詣京西防秋，親兵怨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, three hundred Xuanwu personal troops were always arrogant; Wanrong hated them and sent them to Jingxi autumn defense—the personal troops resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong sent three hundred unruly personal troops to the west; they resented it.

sentences.zh: 大將韓惟清、張彥琳誘親兵作亂，攻萬榮，萬榮擊破之。

translations.literal: Great generals Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin induced the personal troops to rebel, attacked Wanrong; Wanrong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin led the mutiny; Wanrong defeated them.

sentences.zh: 親兵掠而潰，多奔宋州，宋州刺史劉逸准厚撫之。

translations.literal: Personal troops plundered and fled, many running to Songzhou; Songzhou prefect Liu Yizhun comforted them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Mutineers fled to Songzhou where Liu Yizhun sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 惟清奔鄭州，彥琳奔東都。

translations.literal: Weiqing fled to Zhengzhou; Yanlin fled to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing fled to Zhengzhou; Yanlin to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 萬榮悉誅亂者妻子數千人。

translations.literal: Wanrong executed the rebels' wives and children several thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong executed thousands of the rebels' families.

sentences.zh: 有軍士數人呼於市曰：「今夕兵大至，城當破！」

translations.literal: Several soldiers cried in the market: "Tonight great troops arrive—the city will fall!"
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers shouted in the market that the city would fall that night.

sentences.zh: 萬榮收斬之，奏稱劉士寧所為。

translations.literal: Wanrong seized and beheaded them, memorializing that it was Liu Shining's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong executed them and blamed Liu Shining.

sentences.zh: 庚子，徙士寧於郴州。

translations.literal: Day geng-zi; Shining was moved to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the geng-zi day Shining was exiled to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 欽州蠻酋黃少卿反，圍州城，邕管經略使孫公器奏請發嶺南兵救之。

translations.literal: Qinzhou barbarian chieftain Huang Shaoqing rebelled, besieged the prefectural city; Yong-Guan frontier commissioner Sun Gongqi memorialized requesting southern troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaoqing of Qinzhou rebelled; Sun Gongqi asked for Lingnan troops.

sentences.zh: 上不許，遣中使諭解之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit, sent a palace envoy to instruct and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused troops and sent an envoy to mediate.

sentences.zh: 陸贄上言：「鄭禮赦下已近半年，而竄謫者尚未沾恩。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi submitted: "The Zhengli amnesty was issued nearly half a year ago, yet the banished have not yet received grace."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said the amnesty had not reached exiles.

sentences.zh: 乃為三狀擬進。

translations.literal: Then drafted three memorials for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted three lists of exiles to restore.

sentences.zh: 上使謂之曰：「故事，左降官准赦量移，不過三五百里，今所擬稍似超越，又多近兵馬及當路州縣，事恐非便。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent to tell him: "By precedent, demoted officials on amnesty are moved at most three to five hundred li; what is drafted now seems slightly to exceed, and many are near armies and key prefectures—affairs may not be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said exiles should move only three to five hundred li, not near armies.

sentences.zh: 贄復上言，以為：「王者待人以誠，有責怒而無猜嫌，有懲沮而無怨忌。

translations.literal: Zhi again submitted, holding that: "Sage kings treat people with sincerity—there is reproach and anger but no suspicion, punishment and discouragement but no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi argued the throne should trust and rehabilitate exiles.

sentences.zh: 斥遠以儆其不恪，甄恕以勉其自新；

translations.literal: Sending far to warn their lack of respect, discerning forgiveness to encourage their self-renewal;
translations.idiomatic: Exile warns; mercy encourages reform;

sentences.zh: 不儆則浸及威刑，不勉而復加黜削，雖屢進退，俱非愛憎。

translations.literal: if not warned then gradually reaching severe punishment, if not encouraged then again adding demotion and cutting—though repeatedly advancing and retreating, neither is love or hate.
translations.idiomatic: without either, punishment escalates without malice.

sentences.zh: 行法乃暫使左迂，念材而漸加進敘，又知復用，誰不增修！

translations.literal: Applying law is temporarily to make them go left and distant; thinking of talent then gradually adding advancement—also knowing restoration, who would not increase cultivation!
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is temporary; knowing they may return, men will reform.

sentences.zh: 何憂乎亂常，何患乎蓄憾！

translations.literal: Why worry about disorder of constants, why fear stored resentment!
translations.idiomatic: Why fear rebellion or grudges?

sentences.zh: 如或以其貶黜，便謂奸凶，恆處防閒之中，長從擯棄之例，則是悔過者無由自補，蘊才者終不見伸。

translations.literal: If because they were demoted and banished one then calls them treacherous and wicked, always placed in guard and seclusion, long following the example of casting away—then those who repent have no way to repair themselves, those who store talent finally are not extended.
translations.idiomatic: If exiles are forever suspect, the repentant cannot serve again.

sentences.zh: 凡人之情，窮則思變，含淒貪亂，或起於茲。

translations.literal: Generally human feeling—extreme then thinks of change; containing grief and greedy for disorder, sometimes arising from this.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate men turn to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今若所移不過三五百里，則有疆域不離於本道，風土反惡於舊州，徒有徙家之勞，是增移配之擾。

translations.literal: Now if movement is not more than three to five hundred li, then territorial boundaries do not leave the original circuit, wind and soil are worse than the old prefecture—only the toil of moving house, increasing the trouble of reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Short moves only burden exiles without helping.

sentences.zh: 又，當今郡府，多有軍兵，所在封疆，少無館驛，示人疑慮，體又非弘。

translations.literal: Moreover present commanderies mostly have armies; everywhere on the borders few lack post stations—showing people suspicion, the substance again not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Moves near armies and posts signal distrust.

sentences.zh: 乞更賜裁審。」

translations.literal: Request further imperial judgment and review.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 上性猜忌，不委任臣下，官無大小，必自選而用之，宰相進擬，少所稱可；

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was suspicious, not entrusting ministers below; offices great or small, he must himself select and employ; chief ministers' forwarded nominations were rarely approved;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor distrusted ministers and picked every official himself.

sentences.zh: 及群臣一有譴責，往往終身不復收用；

translations.literal: whenever ministers once suffered reprimand, often they were never again employed in life;
translations.idiomatic: Once punished, an official was rarely reused;

sentences.zh: 好以辯給取人，不得敦實之士；

translations.literal: he liked to take people by eloquence, not obtaining solid and honest scholars;
translations.idiomatic: he favored glib men over solid talent;

sentences.zh: 艱於進用，群材滯淹。

translations.literal: hard in advancing employment—many talents stagnated and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: able men were blocked.

sentences.zh: 贄上奏諫，其略曰：「夫登進以懋庸，黜退以懲過，二者迭用，理如循環。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted remonstrance, in summary: "Advancement is to reward merit, demotion to punish fault—both used in turn, principle like cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi said promotion and demotion should cycle like the seasons.

sentences.zh: 進而有過則示懲，懲而改修則復進，既不廢法，亦無棄人，雖纖介必懲而用材不匱。

translations.literal: Advance yet with fault then show punishment; punished yet reform then again advance—neither abandoning law nor abandoning men; though minute must punish, yet employing talent is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Punish faults but reuse the reformed.

sentences.zh: 故能使黜退者克勵以求復，登進者警飭而恪居，上無滯疑，下無蓄怨。」

translations.literal: Thus can make the demoted strive to seek restoration, the advanced warn and restrain and respectfully dwell—above no stagnant suspicion, below no stored resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Then none harbor lasting resentment.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「明主不以辭盡人，不以意選士，如或好善而不擇所用，悅言而不驗所行，進退隨愛憎之情，離合系異同之趣，是由捨繩墨而意裁曲直，棄權衡而手揣重輕，雖甚精微，不能無謬。」

translations.literal: Also said: "Bright rulers do not exhaust men with words, do not select scholars by mood; if one likes the good yet does not choose what is used, delights in words yet does not verify conduct—advance and retreat follow love and hate, union and separation tie to sameness and difference: this is to abandon plumb line and willfully cut crooked and straight, discard balance and hand-weigh heavy and light—even if very fine, cannot be without error."
translations.idiomatic: Rulers must judge deeds, not eloquence or whim.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「中人以上，迭有所長，苟區別得宜，付授當器，各適其性，各宣其能，及乎合以成功，亦與全才無異。

translations.literal: Also said: "Above average men each have strengths; if distinction is fitting and entrustment matches vessel, each suits his nature, each displays his ability—when combined to success, it also differs not from full talent.
translations.idiomatic: Use each man's strength and the whole succeeds.

sentences.zh: 但在明鑒大度，御之有道而已。」

translations.literal: Only in bright discernment and great breadth, governing them with the Way."
translations.idiomatic: That requires magnanimous leadership.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「以一言稱愜為能而不核虛實，以一事違忤為咎而不考忠邪，其稱愜則付任逾涯，不思其所不及，其違忤則罪責過當，不恕其所不能，是以職司之內無成功，君臣之際無定分。」

translations.literal: Also said: "Taking one pleasing phrase as ability without examining truth and falsehood, taking one matter of offense as fault without examining loyal or treacherous—the pleasing then entrustment exceeds bounds, not thinking what is not reached; the offensive then guilt and blame exceed measure, not forgiving what cannot be done—thus within offices no success, between ruler and minister no fixed division."
translations.idiomatic: Praise and blame must follow facts, not moods.

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 贄又請均節財賦，凡六條：

translations.literal: Zhi also requested equal regulation of wealth and levies—six articles in all:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi proposed six fiscal reforms:

sentences.zh: 其一，論兩稅之弊，其略曰：「舊制賦役之法，曰租、調、庸。

translations.literal: First, discussing the two-tax system's defects, in summary: "The old system's levy method was called zu, diao, and yong.
translations.idiomatic: First, on the two-tax system's flaws versus the old zu-diao-yong system.

sentences.zh: 丁男一人受田百畝、歲輸粟二石，謂之租。

translations.literal: One adult male received a hundred mu of land, yearly delivering two shi of grain—called zu.
translations.idiomatic: Each man received land and paid grain rent (zu).

sentences.zh: 每戶各隨土宜出絹若綾若絁共二丈，綿三兩，不蠶之土輸布二丈五尺，麻三斤，謂之調。

translations.literal: Each household according to local suitability produced silk or damask or bo totaling two zhang, cotton three liang; where no sericulture, cloth two zhang five chi, hemp three jin—called diao.
translations.idiomatic: Households paid textiles (diao).

sentences.zh: 每丁歲役，則收其庸，日准絹三尺，謂之庸。

translations.literal: Each ding yearly corvée—then collected their yong, daily standard silk three chi—called yong.
translations.idiomatic: Each man owed labor, commuted to silk (yong).

sentences.zh: 天下為家，法制均一，雖欲轉徙，莫容其奸，故人無搖心而事有定制。

translations.literal: All under Heaven as one family, laws and institutions uniformly one; though wishing to move, none could hide wickedness—thus people had no shaking heart and affairs had fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Uniform law kept people settled and fraud rare.

sentences.zh: 及羯胡亂華，兆庶雲擾，版圖墮於避地，賦法壞於奉軍。

translations.literal: When Jiehu disturbed China, the myriad masses were cloud-turbulent; maps and registers fell to fleeing places, levy law ruined by supply armies.
translations.idiomatic: The An Lushan rebellion destroyed the old system.

sentences.zh: 建中之初，再造百度，執事者知弊之宜革而所作兼失其原，知簡之可從而所操不得其要。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, remaking the hundred measures, those in charge knew defects should be reformed yet what was done together lost the root; knew simplicity could be followed yet what was grasped did not get the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong reformers knew change was needed but botched it.

sentences.zh: 凡欲拯其弊，須窮致弊之由，時弊則但理其時，法弊則全革其法，所為必當，其悔乃亡。

translations.literal: Generally wishing to save defects, must exhaust tracing defect's source; time's defect then only order the time, law's defect then wholly reform the law—what is done must be fitting, then regret is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Fix the root cause—time-bound ills need timely fixes, legal ills need new law.

sentences.zh: 兵興以來，供億無度，此乃時弊，非法弊也。

translations.literal: Since military rise, supply and expenditure without measure—this is time's defect, not law's defect.
translations.idiomatic: Post-rebellion spending was a crisis, not a flaw in zu-diao-yong itself.

sentences.zh: 而遽更租、庸、調法，分遣使者，搜擿郡邑，校驗簿書，每州取大歷中一年科率最多者以為兩稅定額。

translations.literal: Yet hastily changing zu, diao, yong law, separately dispatching envoys, searching prefectures and districts, checking ledgers—each prefecture took the Dali year with highest levy as two-tax fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: They replaced it with the two-tax system based on peak Dali-era levies.

sentences.zh: 夫財之所生，必因人力，故先王之制賦入，必以丁夫為本。

translations.literal: Wealth produced must follow human labor; therefore former kings' levy design must take adult males as root.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue must rest on labor, not assets alone.

sentences.zh: 不以務穡增其稅，不以輟稼減其租，則播種多；

translations.literal: Not because tending crops increase their tax, not because stopping crops reduce their rent—then sowing is more;
translations.idiomatic: Do not tax farming effort away;

sentences.zh: 不以殖產厚其征，不以流寓免其調，則地著固；

translations.literal: not because multiplying estates thicken their levy, not because wanderers escape their diao—then settling on land is firm;
translations.idiomatic: do not let wanderers escape duty;

sentences.zh: 不以飭勵重其役，不以窳怠蠲其庸，則功力勤。

translations.literal: not because exhortation and encouragement weight their corvée, not because slackness and idleness exempt their yong—then labor power is diligent.
translations.idiomatic: do not exempt the idle from corvée.

sentences.zh: 如是，故人安其居，盡其力矣。

translations.literal: If thus, then people secure their dwellings and exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Then people work in peace.

sentences.zh: 兩稅之立，惟以資產為宗，不以丁身為本。

translations.literal: The two-tax establishment takes only assets as principle, not persons as root.
translations.idiomatic: The two-tax system taxes wealth, not people.

sentences.zh: 曾不寤資產之中，有藏於襟懷囊篋，物雖貴而人莫能窺；

translations.literal: Never awakening that among assets some hide in bosom and bag—things though precious and people cannot peep;
translations.idiomatic: Hidden wealth escapes assessment;

sentences.zh: 其積於場圃囷倉，直雖輕而眾以為富流通蕃息之貨，數雖寡而計日收贏；

translations.literal: those piled in yards and granaries—value though light yet masses think rich; circulating and breeding goods—numbers though few yet daily profit reckoned;
translations.idiomatic: visible grain is taxed while mobile trade is miscounted;

sentences.zh: 有廬舍器用之資，價雖高而終歲無利。

translations.literal: having hut and implement resources—price though high yet year-long no profit.
translations.idiomatic: expensive tools with no income are overtaxed.

sentences.zh: 如此之比，其流實繁，一概計估算緡，宜其失平長偽。

translations.literal: Comparisons like this, their flow truly numerous—altogether calculating and estimating in strings of cash, fitting that imbalance and long falsity.
translations.idiomatic: Uniform cash valuation breeds fraud.

sentences.zh: 由是務輕資而樂轉徙者，恆脫於徭稅；

translations.literal: Thus those who pursue light assets and delight in moving often escape corvée and tax;
translations.idiomatic: Those who move lightly escape tax;

sentences.zh: 敦本業而樹居產者，每困於徵求。

translations.literal: those who consolidate root occupation and build settled property are each trapped in collection.
translations.idiomatic: those who stay are squeezed.

sentences.zh: 此乃誘之為奸，驅之避役，力用不得不弛，賦入不得不闕。

translations.literal: This is inducing them to wickedness, driving them to avoid service—labor power must slacken, levy intake must lack.
translations.idiomatic: The system rewards evasion and drains the diligent.

sentences.zh: 復以創製之首，不務齊平，供應有煩簡之殊，牧守有能否之異，所在徭賦，輕重相懸，所遣使臣，意見各異，計奏一定，有加無除。

translations.literal: Also at the creation's head, not striving for equality; supply had simple and complex differences, shepherds and guards had able and unable differences—wherever corvée and levies, light and heavy hung apart; envoys sent, opinions each different; memorialized fix once, additions without subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset the system was unequal: supplies varied in burden, prefects in competence, and local levies in weight; each envoy interpreted policy differently, and once quotas were set, increases were never removed.

sentences.zh: 又大歷中供軍、進奉之類，既收入兩稅，今於兩稅之外，復又並存，望稍行均減，以救凋殘。」

translations.literal: Also Dali-era army supply and tribute types, already received into two-tax—now outside two-tax again coexist; hope slightly to carry out equal reduction to save the withered and crippled."
translations.idiomatic: Old surcharges remained atop the new tax—he asked to cut them."

sentences.zh: 其二，請二稅以布帛為額，不計錢數。

translations.literal: Second, request two-tax take silk and cloth as quota, not counting cash.
translations.idiomatic: Second, set the two-tax quota in cloth, not coin.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「凡國之賦稅，必量人之力，任土之宜，故所入者惟布、麻、繒、纊與百谷而已。

translations.literal: In summary: "Generally state's levies must measure men's strength, follow soil's suitability—therefore intake is only cloth, hemp, silk, floss, and hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes should be paid in grain and cloth suited to the land.

sentences.zh: 先王懼物之貴賤失平，而人之交易難准，又定泉布之法以節輕重之宜，斂散弛張，必由於是。

translations.literal: Former kings feared things' dear and cheap losing balance and men's trade hard to standardize—also fixed coin-cloth law to moderate light and heavy suitability; gathering, dispersing, loosening, tightening must go through this.
translations.idiomatic: The state should control coinage to stabilize prices.

sentences.zh: 蓋御財之大柄，為國之利權，守之在官，不以任下。

translations.literal: This is holding wealth's great handle, state's profit power—keeping it in office, not entrusting below.
translations.idiomatic: Coinage must stay in government hands.

sentences.zh: 然則谷帛者，人之所為也；

translations.literal: Then grain and cloth are what men make;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and cloth are produced by the people;

sentences.zh: 錢貨者，官之所為也。

translations.literal: coin and goods are what office makes.
translations.idiomatic: coin is made by the state.

sentences.zh: 是以國朝著令，租出谷，庸出絹，調出繒、纊、布，曷嘗有禁人鑄錢而以錢為賦者也！

translations.literal: Therefore the dynasty's established orders: rent yields grain, yong yields silk, diao yields silk, floss, and cloth—when ever was people forbidden to cast coin yet take coin as levy!
translations.idiomatic: Never before were taxes levied in coin alone.

sentences.zh: 今之兩稅，獨異舊章，但估資產為差，便以錢穀定稅，臨時折征雜物，每歲色目頗殊，唯計求得之利宜，靡論供辦之難易。

translations.literal: Today's two-tax alone differs from old statutes—only estimating assets as grades, then fixing tax in cash and grain; at time converting and levying mixed goods, yearly categories quite different—only calculating obtained profit and suitability, not discussing supply's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The two-tax forces cash payment and arbitrary surcharges.

sentences.zh: 所征非所業，所業非所征，遂或增價以買其所無，減價以賣其所有，一增一減，耗損已多。

translations.literal: What is levied is not their occupation; their occupation is not what is levied—then some raise price to buy what they lack, reduce price to sell what they have; one raise one reduce, loss and waste already much.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers must buy and sell at a loss to pay tax.

sentences.zh: 望勘會諸州初納兩稅年絹布，定估比類當今時價，加賤減貴，酌取其中，總計合稅之錢，折為布帛之數。」

translations.literal: Hope to examine all prefectures' first two-tax year silk and cloth, fix estimate compared to present prices, add to cheap and reduce dear, take the middle, total combined tax cash, convert to cloth number."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed converting tax quotas back to silk at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「夫地力之生物有大限，取之有度，用之有節，則常足。

translations.literal: Also said: "Earth's power in producing things has great limit; taking has measure, using has regulation—then constantly sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Production is finite; thrift brings sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 取之無度，用之無節，則常不足。

translations.literal: Taking without measure, using without regulation—then constantly insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Waste brings shortage.

sentences.zh: 生物之豐敗由天，用物之多少由人。

translations.literal: Things' abundance and failure are from Heaven; things' use much or little are from men.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests are heaven's; spending is man's.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王立程，量入為出，雖遇災難，下無困窮。

translations.literal: Therefore sage kings establish measures, measure intake to set outflow—even meeting disaster, below no distress and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings spent within revenue.

sentences.zh: 理化既衰，則乃反是，量出為入，不恤所無。

translations.literal: When order and transformation declined, then it reversed—measure outflow to set intake, not pitying what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Decadent rulers spent first and taxed after.

sentences.zh: 桀用天下而不足，湯用七十里而有餘，是乃用之盈虛，在節與不節耳。」

translations.literal: Jie used all under Heaven yet insufficient; Tang used seventy li yet had surplus—this is use's full and empty, in regulating or not regulating."
translations.idiomatic: Jie was prodigal; Tang was frugal."

sentences.zh: 其三，論長吏以增戶、加稅、辟田為課績，其略曰：「長人者罕能推忠恕易地之情，體至公徇國之意，迭行小惠，競誘姦□，以傾奪鄰境為智能，以招萃逋逃為理化，捨彼適此者既為新收而有復，倏往忽來者又以復業而見優。

translations.literal: Third, discussing long officials taking increased households, added tax, and opened fields as examination achievement, in summary: "Those who govern people rarely can extend loyal-forgiveness and putting-oneself-in-others' place feeling, embody utmost public and devote-to-state intent—repeatedly practicing small favors, competing to entice the wicked, taking overthrowing neighboring borders as intelligence, gathering fugitives as ordering transformation; those leaving there for here are already new intake with reduction, those suddenly coming and going also because returning to occupation are seen as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Third, on perverse incentives for local officials: they lured migrants and fugitives for merit while punishing stable taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 唯懷土安居，首末不遷者，則使之日重，斂之日加。

translations.literal: Only those cherishing land and secure dwelling, beginning and end not moving—then make their day heavier, collection day added.
translations.idiomatic: Settled farmers bore heavier taxes than drifters.

sentences.zh: 是令地著之人恆代惰游賦役，則何異驅之轉徙，教之澆訛。

translations.literal: This is making settled people constantly replace idle wanderers' levies—what difference from driving them to move and teaching them corruption.
translations.idiomatic: It was like driving the honest into exile.

sentences.zh: 此由牧宰不克弘通，各私所部之過也。」

translations.literal: This is because shepherds cannot broadly comprehend, each privatizing his department's faults."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects served their own stats, not the realm.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「立法齊人，久無不弊，理之者若不知維御損益之宜，則巧偽萌生，恆因沮勸而滋矣。

translations.literal: Also said: "Establishing law to equalize people, long without no defect; ordering it, if not knowing the art of maintaining, controlling, benefiting and harming, then craft and falsity arise, constantly because discouragement and encouragement that they grow.
translations.idiomatic: Laws need adjusting as abuses appear.

sentences.zh: 請申命有司，詳定考績。

translations.literal: Request again command the offices, detail fix examination records.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to reform performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 若當管之內，人益阜殷，所定稅額有餘，任其據戶口均減，以減數多少為考課等差。

translations.literal: If within jurisdiction people grow prosperous, fixed tax quota has surplus, allow according to households evenly reduce—the reduction amount's more or less as examination grades.
translations.idiomatic: Reward officials who cut taxes when population grew.

sentences.zh: 其當管稅物通比，每戶十分減三者為上課，減二者次焉，減一者又次焉。

translations.literal: Within jurisdiction tax goods compared, per household ten parts reduce three is upper grade, reduce two next, reduce one again next.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-percent cuts ranked merit.

sentences.zh: 如或人多流亡，加稅見戶，比校殿罰亦如之。」

translations.literal: If people greatly flee and visible households' tax is added, comparing grades punishment likewise."
translations.idiomatic: Penalize those who taxed the remnant harder."

sentences.zh: 其四，論稅限迫促，其略曰：「建官立國，所以養人也；

translations.literal: Fourth, discussing tax deadlines pressed tight, in summary: "Establishing offices and founding state is to nourish people;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, on harsh tax deadlines:

sentences.zh: 賦人取財，所以資國也。

translations.literal: levying people to take wealth is to fund the state.
translations.idiomatic: taxes fund the state but must not ruin the people.

sentences.zh: 明君不厚其所資而害其所養，故必先人事而借其暇力，先家給而斂其餘財。」

translations.literal: Bright rulers do not enrich what they fund and harm what they nourish—therefore first human affairs then borrow their spare strength, first household supply then gather remaining wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Tax after the harvest, not before.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「蠶事方興，已輸縑稅，農功未艾，遽斂谷租。

translations.literal: Also said: "Silkworm affairs just rising, already delivering silk tax; farming work not ended, hastily collecting grain rent.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was taken before cocoons; grain before harvest.

sentences.zh: 上司之繩責既嚴，下吏之威暴愈促，有者急賣而耗其半直，無者求假而費其倍酬。

translations.literal: Superiors' rope of blame already strict, lower clerks' violent oppression more urgent—those with goods urgently sell and lose half value; those without seek loans and spend double compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Forced sales at ruinous prices followed.

sentences.zh: 望更詳定徵稅期限。」

translations.literal: Hope further detail fix levy collection deadlines."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for later deadlines."

sentences.zh: 其五，請以稅茶錢置義倉以備水旱，其略曰：「古稱九年、六年之蓄者，率土臣庶通為之計耳，固非獨豐公庚，不及編□也。

translations.literal: Fifth, request using tea-tax money to establish charity granaries for flood and drought, in summary: "Ancient called nine-year, six-year storage—realm's subjects common plan, not only Duke of Zhou's granaries not reaching registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, use tea tax for charity granaries as of old.

sentences.zh: 近者有司奏請稅茶，歲約得五十萬貫，元敕令貯戶部，用救百姓凶饑。

translations.literal: Recently offices memorialized tea tax, yearly about 500,000 strings; original edict ordered storage at Ministry of Revenue to relieve people's famine.
translations.idiomatic: Tea tax was supposed to fund disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 今以蓄糧，適副前旨。」

translations.literal: Now using it to store grain suits the former intent."
translations.idiomatic: Storing grain matched that intent."

sentences.zh: 其六，論兼併之家，私斂重於公稅，其略曰：「今京畿之內，每田一畝，官稅五升，而私家收租殆有畝至一石者，是二十倍於官稅也。

translations.literal: Sixth, discussing consolidated households—private rent heavier than public tax, in summary: "Now within the capital, each mu of field, official tax five sheng, yet private rent collection nearly has per mu up to one shi—this is twenty times official tax.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, on landlords: private rent was twenty times the state tax.

sentences.zh: 降及中等，租猶半之。

translations.literal: Descending to middle grades, rent still half that.
translations.idiomatic: Even middling rents doubled the state levy.

sentences.zh: 夫土地王者之所有，耕稼農夫之所為，而兼併之徒，居然受利。」

translations.literal: Land is the king's possession; plowing and harvest farmers' doing—yet consolidators calmly receive profit."
translations.idiomatic: Land belongs to the throne, yet magnates took the profit.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「望凡所佔田，約為條限，裁減租價，務利貧人。

translations.literal: Also said: "Hope all occupied fields, about set limits, cut reduce rent price, strive to benefit poor people.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to cap rents and protect tenants.

sentences.zh: 法貴必行，慎在深刻，裕其制以便俗，嚴其令以懲違，微損有餘，稍優不足，失不損富，優可賑窮，此乃古者安富恤窮之善經，不可捨也。」

translations.literal: Law values must be carried out; caution lies in depth and severity; broaden its regulation to suit custom, strict its orders to punish violation; slight loss to the surplus, slight favor to the insufficient—loss does not harm the rich, favor can relieve the poor—this is the ancients' good constant of securing the rich and pitying the poor, cannot be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Moderate rent cuts would aid the poor without ruining the rich."
